About Us

About AllUnity

AllUnity is a regulated e-money institute building Europe’s digital payments infrastructure for instant cross-border payments, digital asset markets, and seamless liquidity flows. Established by DWS, Flow Traders, and Galaxy, AllUnity delivers fully backed, MiCAR-compliant stablecoins (EURAU, CHFAU and SEKAU) that provide regulatory certainty and robust reserve backing for secure, frictionless capital movement across markets.

About the Role

We are looking for a Risk Specialist with experience in structured risk management within a regulated financial services environment and a strong interest or exposure to blockchain-based products. The role focuses on risk framework development, new product and change assessments, and technology-related risk analysis in a digital asset context.

You will act as a key contributor to the Institute’s second-line risk function, supporting the evaluation of new blockchain integrations, product developments and outsourcing arrangements under MiCA and DORA. The role combines traditional operational risk management with digital asset specific risk considerations.

You will manage defined risk workstreams, particularly in the assessment of new blockchain integrations and product developments.

Key Responsibilities

1. Core Risk Management & Governance

  • Conduct inherent and residual risk assessments in line with the Institute’s risk methodology
  • Maintain and enhance the risk inventory, including control mapping and documentation standards
  • Assess control design and effectiveness across operational and technology-related processes
  • Monitor KRIs and risk appetite thresholds, including follow-up and escalation where required
  • Support tracking and monitoring of recovery indicators and related governance processes
  • Contribute to material change assessments and structured risk papers for management

2. New Product & Process Risk (NPP)

  • Perform end-to-end risk assessments for new blockchain integrations (e.g., L1/L2 chains, bridge solutions)
  • Assess impact on existing operational processes, governance structures and control frameworks
  • Evaluate smart contract-related risk exposure at a conceptual level (e.g., mint/burn controls, upgradeability, governance mechanisms)
  • Identify operational, ICT, outsourcing and concentration risks arising from new initiatives
  • Support the preparation of clear, decision-ready risk assessments for internal approval committees

3. Technology, ICT & Outsourcing Risk (MiCA / DORA)

  • Support alignment of ICT and outsourcing risk management with MiCA and DORA requirements
  • Evaluate third-party providers (e.g., custody, bridge, oracle and technology providers) from a risk and criticality perspective
  • Assess resilience, dependency, concentration and exit strategy considerations
  • Contribute to operational resilience testing and scenario development
  • Ensure technology and outsourcing risks are consistently reflected in the overall risk profile

4. Digital Asset Risk Structuring

  • Translate technical setups into structured, risk-relevant documentation
  • Identify key risk drivers such as governance risk, third-party dependency and single points of failure
  • Challenge control design constructively and propose practical mitigation measures
  • Support stress scenario development (e.g., bridge exploit, de-pegging, chain halt)

Key Requirements

Experience

  • 4 - 6 years of professional experience in Risk Management, Operational Risk, Internal Audit or Risk Advisory
  • Experience in a regulated financial services environment (e.g., bank, EMI, fintech or comparable institution)
  • Practical exposure to risk assessments, control evaluations and governance processes
  • Experience supporting new product approvals or material change assessments is a strong advantage

Technical & Regulatory Knowledge

  • Solid understanding of risk assessment methodologies (inherent/residual risk, control effectiveness, risk appetite frameworks)
  • Familiarity with blockchain fundamentals (e.g., token issuance, smart contracts, L1/L2 chains, bridge concepts)
  • Understanding of operational and technology risk in digital asset environments
  • Knowledge of MiCA and/or DORA requirements is strongly preferred
  • Awareness of outsourcing and third-party risk principles in regulated institutions

Skills & Working Style

  • Strong analytical and structured thinking
  • Excellent documentation and drafting skills in German & English
  • Proficiency in German is required
  • Ability to translate technical and regulatory topics into clear risk documentation
  • Independent and solution-oriented working style
  • Confidence to challenge constructively while collaborating across functions
  • High attention to detail and ownership mindset

Why You Should Apply

In this role, you will not only monitor risk, you will actively contribute to the development and refinement of the risk framework of a BaFin regulated euro stablecoin institution operating under MiCA and DORA.
You will gain hands-on experience at the intersection of traditional financial risk management and blockchain-based infrastructure, working closely with senior leadership in a highly regulated environment.
This role offers meaningful ownership, regulatory depth and exposure to one of Europe’s most innovative digital financial initiatives.

  • Regular Team Retreats & Offsites
  • Welcome Packages & Company Swag

title: Full Stack Product Engineer (100% Remote - Germany | UK | Ireland)
description:
Build analytics people can trust. Help define what analytics looks like in an AI-first world.

Most analytics platforms ask organisations to trade control for insight.

For almost 20 years, Matomo has shown there is another way: powerful, transparent and trustworthy analytics that respects privacy, gives organisations ownership of their data, and helps people understand what's happening, make better decisions, and improve their work.

More than one million websites use Matomo. That means you'll work on software that is widely used, technically demanding, and close enough to customers that your work has a visible impact. It's a rare opportunity for engineers: solving meaningful, complex product problems while seeing the difference your work makes for customers.

We are independent, profitable, and open source. We are not trying to become a smaller copy of Big Tech analytics platforms. We are building a different kind of analytics company: one where privacy, transparency, customer control, and product quality are part of the core product, not marketing claims.

This role focuses on Matomo Core, the foundation of our product and the platform our open-source users, cloud customers, and wider plugin ecosystem depend on.

If you want unusually high ownership, visible impact, hard product & platform problems, and the opportunity to strengthen a widely used open-source platform, Matomo is worth a serious look.


Why this role matters

Matomo Core is the foundation of our open-source product, cloud platform, plugins, integrations and customer-facing features. 

It has evolved over many years and operates across a wide range of environments, use cases and data volumes. Every improvement to Core benefits customers, open-source users, plugin developers and engineering teams across the Matomo ecosystem. 

We are bringing responsibility for Core into a newly formed European team. You'll help shape how this team works, where it focuses and how it creates the greatest impact across Matomo. 

As a Product Engineer, you’ll help decide where Core can create the greatest impact. That could mean solving a difficult customer problem, strengthening an existing capability, creating a new platform capability, or simplifying the Core platform to make it easier to evolve. 

You’ll work on a mature and technically complex product. The challenge is not simply to preserve what exists. It is to understand why it exists, recognise where it is holding customers or engineers back, and evolve it without disrupting the open-source users, customers, integrations and plugins that already depend on it. 


What you’ll own

You'll own problems, not just code. 

This is not a traditional feature-ticket engineering role. You'll understand customer problems, shape solutions, build across the stack, ship incrementally and continuously improve what you release. AI should be part of your everyday workflow. 

You'll own work from problem to outcome: 

  • Understand the problem before committing to a solution.  

  • Help shape priorities, not just implement them.  

  • Build across the stack wherever the problem takes you.  

  • Ship incrementally and learn from real usage.  

  • Measure outcomes and iterate.  

  • Use AI throughout your workflow. 

    • For senior: You'll help shape what we build, not only how we build it. You'll identify opportunities others haven't seen, influence technical and product direction, and help establish how the Core team operates as it grows. 

    For intermediate: You'll contribute to deciding what we build, working closely with product, engineering and customers rather than simply implementing predefined requirements. You'll own meaningful problems end-to-end while building confidence in navigating ambiguity and product trade-offs. 

    What the work looks like 

    You'll work across the Core platform wherever you can create the greatest impact. 

    Examples include: 

    • Diagnosing and solving complex problems across a large, mature codebase.  

    • Strengthening the security, performance, scalability, reliability and resilience of Matomo.  

    • Protecting the integrity, accuracy and trustworthiness of the data customers rely on.  

    • Strengthen capabilities that support increasingly demanding enterprise use cases.  

    • Building and evolving APIs and platform capabilities used by Matomo plugins and integrations.  

    • Evolving how Matomo handles consent, privacy and responsible data collection. 

    • Advancing server-side tracking, data anonymisation and data-health monitoring. 

    • Enhancing analytics capabilities such as goals, ecommerce reporting and dashboards.

    • Simplifying complex analytics workflows and making powerful functionality easier to use.  

    • Evolving Matomo's design system to create a more consistent and usable product experience. 


How we work

We’re a small team competing with companies many times our size.

That means we optimise for impact.

We value:

  • Customer problems over technical elegance.

  • Shipping over endless planning.

  • Simple solutions over unnecessary complexity.

  • Ownership over handoffs.

  • Iteration over perfection.

  • Clear writing over excessive meetings.

  • Pragmatic engineering over abstract architecture.

  • AI where it helps us move faster.

  • Measuring outcomes over assuming we were right.

    • We care about high standards, but we do not confuse high standards with slow processes. We would rather ship a small useful improvement, learn from it, and improve it than spend months perfecting something before customers see it.

    At the same time, changes to Matomo Core can affect a large number of customers, integrations and plugins. You should be able to move pragmatically while recognising when additional investigation, testing or migration planning is necessary.


What we’re looking for

For senior: You're already operating with a high degree of autonomy. You naturally identify valuable opportunities, make pragmatic decisions in ambiguous situations, and multiply the team's impact through the systems you build, the decisions you influence and the way you approach problems. 

For intermediate: You're already comfortable delivering software independently and are looking to take greater ownership of customer problems, product decisions and technical direction. 

You enjoy building products

You get motivated by solving customer problems and delivering value, not by technical novelty alone.

You care whether people actually use and benefit from what you build. Seeing a feature make a real difference is more rewarding to you than building something technically clever that nobody uses.

You naturally ask:

  • What problem are we solving?

  • Who has this problem?

  • Is this the simplest useful solution?

  • How will we know this made things better?

  • What should we do if the data shows we were wrong?

    • You are comfortable with complex, mature systems

    You do not need every problem to start with a clean architecture or an empty repository.

    You are comfortable tracing behaviour across an unfamiliar codebase, understanding historical constraints, debugging difficult interactions, and making incremental improvements without unnecessary rewrites.

    You can balance immediate customer needs with longer-term platform health. You know when to fix the immediate issue, when to address the underlying cause, and when a broader architectural change is justified.

    You are comfortable across the stack

    You are happy working wherever the problem takes you: frontend, backend, databases, APIs, product flows, documentation, or customer feedback.

    Our stack includes PHP, MySQL, JavaScript, Vue.js, and TypeScript. Exact stack experience is useful, but not required. We care more about your ability to learn, reason, ship, and solve meaningful problems.

    You use AI as part of how you work

    We make heavy use of AI-assisted development throughout our engineering workflow.

    You should already be using AI tools regularly or be strongly motivated to do so. We expect Product Engineers to use AI to increase output and quality.

    AI does not replace your judgment. You remain responsible for product decisions, technical correctness, security, privacy, maintainability, and customer impact.


You’ll probably thrive here if

  • You prefer owning outcomes over receiving detailed tickets.

  • You enjoy solving difficult problems in existing systems as well as building new functionality.

  • You can quickly diagnose complex or intermittent bugs.

  • You can move from customer feedback or operational evidence to investigation, product decision and implementation.

  • You care about reliability, performance and data accuracy, not only visible feature work.

  • You can improve a mature codebase without assuming it needs to be rewritten.

  • You use AI tools heavily and are actively improving how you work with them.

  • You are pragmatic: you can make a focused improvement now while recognising when a deeper change is needed.

  • You can explain technical and product trade-offs clearly.

  • You enjoy working across product, engineering, UX, data and customer feedback.

  • You like small teams where your decisions and output visibly matter.

    • below for intermediate only:

    • You're excited to take on increasingly ambiguous problems.  

      • You want to grow beyond implementation into shaping products and technical decisions. 


You may not enjoy this role if

  • You mainly want to work on new greenfield products.

  • You see maintenance, debugging, reliability or performance work as less valuable than feature development.

  • You want a product manager to define most requirements before you start.

  • You are uncomfortable investigating problems where the cause is initially unclear.

  • You prefer replacing existing systems rather than understanding why they work as they do.

  • You measure success mainly by code quality rather than user or business impact.

  • You are uncomfortable using AI as part of your normal engineering workflow.

  • You need a large team, narrow responsibilities, or highly formal processes to be effective.

  • You prefer polishing a solution extensively before showing it to users.

  • You dislike writing proposals, documentation, or product notes.

  • You are uncomfortable balancing speed, backwards compatibility and long-term platform health.


Remote work

Matomo is a remote company.

We work mostly asynchronously and rely heavily on clear written communication. You should be comfortable working independently, documenting your thinking, and collaborating without needing constant meetings.


Location
100% remote — Germany, UK or Ireland only.

Hiring process

Our process is designed to understand how you think, build, communicate, and use AI in realistic product engineering work.

The process usually includes: Application → Screening → Online aptitude test → People & Culture interview → Technical skills interview → Final technical interview.

We do not expect unpaid multi-day projects. We want to understand how you approach ambiguous problems, make trade-offs, use AI, and ship useful product improvements.


Diversity and Inclusion
InnoCraft (trading as Matomo) values what makes you unique. We’re an inclusive employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, because diverse perspectives help us build better products.

Interested?
If you care about solving meaningful customer problems, improving software that people depend on, working with high ownership, and making privacy-friendly analytics more secure, reliable, accurate and useful, we’d like to hear from you.

description:
VERDANCY
Aachen, Germany (RWTH Aachen) | On-site / Hybrid | Co-Founder / Equity | Deep Tech / AgTech & Biotechnology

**About Verdancy
**Verdancy is a start up in the making from the Schwaneberg Group at the Institute of Biotechnology of RWTH Aachen University. It develops biodegradable additives that make crop-protection products stick to leaves and last longer. Bio-based microgels carry the active substance and release it on demand, while bi-adhesive peptides anchor the microgel to the leaf wax so the coating survives rain — meaning fewer sprays and less pesticide lost to the environment. A second product line uses bifunctional peptides (antimicrobial peptide + anchor) as peptide-based pesticides in their own right, protected by patent EP3261435B1. The entry market is copper fungicide against grapevine downy mildew, where there is no real alternative today, poor rain resistance is a known problem, and the EU is pushing hard to cut copper use.

**The opportunity
**Built on more than 10 years of university research across six projects (€7m raised, TRL 5), the startup is now being further developed by Susanne Braun (CSO, polymer chemist, carrier systems and formulations) and Atul Kumar (CTO, biotechnologist, protein engineering). Verdancy already has a developed business model, funding secured through May 2027 via the Warp Speed Fund of the Materials Lab Incubator (MerLIn), a successful soybean-rust project and a new €2.4m insect-focused project starting January 2027. What's missing is the business development leadership to found the spin-off company and go after an €80B addressable market (€1.2B in the copper segment alone).
Aachen, Germany (RWTH Aachen) | On-site / Hybrid | Co-Founder / Equity | Deep Tech / AgTech & Biotechnology

Fundraising & partnerships

- Develop third-party-funded project relationships and networks alongside the existing €2.4m insect-focused project (starting Jan 2027).

Requirements

Core experience
**- Business development experience, ideally in AgTech, crop protection, biotech, or a related regulated life-sciences market.
- Comfort founding a company out of a university research group and navigating the transition from grant funding to commercial revenue.
Especially valuable
- Familiarity with EU pesticide/crop-protection regulatory approval processes.
- Experience with materials/biotech spin-offs or deep-tech incubators (Verdancy is currently in the Materials Lab Incubator's Warp Speed Fund).
- Existing network among crop-protection companies, distributors or grapevine/viticulture producers.

- Over 10 years and €7m of university research already de-risked the science (TRL-5), with a patented core technology (EP3261435B1) and peer-reviewed publications.

Who We Are

An AI agent that runs a property transaction end to end only works if the data underneath it is available, reliable and governed. That is the job.

Why this role exists

This is the first dedicated data hire in years. The foundations run, the steering is up to you.

While BigQuery already houses most of our data, we still lack key Growth data and a cohesive data governance framework. We need unified definitions, a canonical schema, and a robust semantic layer, enabling Growth, Finance, Ops and Product to self-serve insights efficiently and reliably.

Today the stack holds because individuals across Ops, Growth, Finance and Engineering compensate locally. They learned the quirks and built workarounds. It works, but it is fragile: KPIs drift between tools, tracking breaks silently, costs escalate, and nobody owns the translation between raw engineering data and decision-ready truth.

You will be the single accountable owner of that layer. Not a support function, not a ticketing desk, not a BI factory.

What you will own

Canonical models and metric definitions. A documented semantic layer with canonical entities (Buyer, Seller, Asset, Agent) and Bronze / Silver / Gold layers. Clear contracts between what Engineering exposes and what each function consumes, so that KPI debates are aligned on the same metric.

Self-serve enablement. The submerged part of the iceberg: clean models, consistent BI primitives, row- and column-level security, so Ops, Growth, Finance and Account Managers build their own dashboards without compromising on accuracy.

Analytics and tracking governance. The global event taxonomy and tracking roadmap, a hybrid client-side and server-side event strategy, consistent sync across CRMs and marketing platforms, and GDPR consent flows by design, so acquisition spend runs on attribution we can trust.

Platform reliability, safety and cost. Standards set once rather than team by team: tested and versioned transformations, monitoring of freshness, failures and usage, sane ingestion patterns (read replicas, CDC, batch), and no production code path depending on BI tables.

Data and AI driving decisions. Our internal AI tooling already queries the data warehouse for analyses. What’s missing is the core foundation: standardized metric definitions, reusable logic, and pre-computed data models.

What success looks like after 12 months

  • One documented event taxonomy, actually used by Engineering, Growth and CRM.

  • One semantic layer where every shared KPI has a single definition, a single owner and a version history. New joiners understand the data model in days, not months.

  • Published freshness and failure SLAs, an explicit ingestion topology, and no production path depending on BI tables.

  • Ops, Growth, Finance and AMs build most of their recurring dashboards themselves, and AI agents query the data layer safely through curated MCPs.

  • Growth attribution is trustworthy enough that annual acquisition spend decisions are defensible end to end.

What we are looking for

  • 7+ years as a Data, Analytics or Platform Engineer, ideally including a stint at a fast-moving consumer or marketplace company. Staff or Lead exposure expected.

  • Hands-on with the modern data stack: BigQuery (or Snowflake, Redshift), dbt or equivalent, advanced SQL and data modeling, Python for pipelines, orchestration (Airflow, Dagster, Prefect).

  • You have shipped event tracking and instrumentation in production, end to end: taxonomy, client and server-side events, attribution, GDPR-compliant opt-out, propagation downstream.

  • Comfortable with ingestion patterns (Fivetran, Airbyte, CDC), reverse-ETL (Hightouch, Census, Segment), and access governance (IAM, row- and column-level security, PII tagging).

  • You have built and owned a semantic or metrics layer, and you can arbitrate metric definitions with Finance, Ops and Growth without flinching.

  • You treat AI agents as first-class data consumers: exposing data through MCPs, semantic APIs or text-to-SQL, with proper guardrails.

  • Strong ownership: you write the standards, defend them, and fix what is broken without waiting for permission.

  • A clear communicator who turns "ping the data person" rituals into self-serve handoffs.

  • Fluent in English and French.

The honest trade-off

There is no data team to manage, and none planned in the short term. You get real autonomy and a direct line to the founders and function leads, in exchange for building alone before maybe building a team. At a comparable proptech you would join an existing team and an existing roadmap. Here, what a metric means at Zefir is not decided yet, and you are the one who decides it.

ScorePlay is the AI-powered media infrastructure for sports, built to automate the content operations behind the world's biggest sports organizations. We work with 300+ leagues, competitions, teams and broadcasters – including Ligue 1 and Premier League clubs, NBA and NFL teams, the Tour de France, the Australian Open, and leading bodies like UEFA and FIBA – helping them turn every moment on and off the field into high-value, structured content. Our platform brings all their media into one place and makes it effortless to find, edit and share in seconds.

Founded in 2021, we’re a 50-person team based between New York and Paris, growing 2x year over year with 98% retention. We’ve raised $20M+ from top investors including Alexis Ohanian and Harry Stebbing’s 20VC and elite athletes like Kevin Durant, Raphaël Varane, Mario Götze, Nico Rosberg and Giannis Antetokounmpo.

If you’re passionate about sports and thrive in fast-paced environments - and you want to help shape how the next generation of fans experience sports, you’re in the right place. We’re on track to become the global leader in sports media, and this is definitely the best time to join our adventure.

 

Location: Hybrid from Paris or full remote

Role Overview

ScorePlay signs deals with some of the biggest organizations in sports, and every one of them starts with a contract. We are hiring a Commercial Contracts Counsel to own that: redlines, negotiations, signatures, the whole thing. You work directly with Lou, our General Counsel, and are the first point of contact for Sales on contracts.

What you will do

1. Contracts

  • You review, redline and negotiate the agreements that close our deals: MSAs, service agreements, order forms, SOWs, NDAs and DPAs, with clubs, leagues, federations, broadcasters and brands, often across several countries.

  • Sales comes to you when a deal is stuck on terms, and your job is to unstick it: fast turnaround, pragmatic fallbacks, and the judgement to know when a point is worth holding.

  • You partner with Sales, Finance, RevOps and Customer Success so contract terms match how the deal is actually priced, booked and delivered.

  • You take a share of vendor and partner agreements alongside Lou, split based on what is moving and where you want to build depth.

2. Tools, processes and enablement

  • We use AI heavily in contract work: drafting, first-pass reviews, summarizing counterparty terms. We want someone who genuinely enjoys this and keeps looking for a smarter way to handle the repetitive part.

  • Our legal playbook is young. You execute it, then you help Lou refine it with what you see in real negotiations.

3. Privacy and security

  • You contribute to customer security, privacy and vendor due-diligence questionnaires, and to DPA and international transfer questions. The heart of the role is contracts, with room to grow into broader compliance work if that interests you.

What we are looking for

  • You know commercial contracts inside out. 3 to 5 years of experience, most of it in-house, with contracts at the core of what you did.

  • You work autonomously. Give you an MSA or a set of customer redlines and you come back with a position, a fallback and a recommendation.

  • You ship fast. A solid answer today beats a perfect one on Friday, and you're comfortable making the call at 80% certainty.

  • You're resourceful. When something is unclear, you dig, you ask, you find a way, rather than waiting for perfect instructions.

  • You like helping people win. Supporting a Sales team means being responsive, available, and genuinely happy when a deal signs because of your work.

  • You're excited by AI. You already use it in your legal work, or you can't wait to, and you keep looking for smarter ways to handle the repetitive parts.

What’s fun about this role

  • You negotiate international contracts with some of the biggest names in sports: clubs, leagues, federations and broadcasters on every continent.

  • As our first commercial counsel, you own your function and you're the main partner of the Sales team on both sides of the Atlantic.

  • You sit in sales calls with senior stakeholders at major sports organizations, on deals worth USD 50k to 500k a year. When a deal closes, you're usually one of the key players who made it work.

  • Small team, short loops. You'll have the opportunity to bring ideas to the table, build playbooks, experiment with AI and new tools, and learn a ton along the way.

We know many people hesitate to apply if they don’t meet every single requirement on a job description. If you’re interested in ScorePlay but not sure you tick all the boxes, we’d still love to hear from you, this could be the start of a great long-term collaboration.

title: Location Data engineer
description:
We are seeking a highly skilled Location Data Engineer to join our team. In this role, you will work with large-scale datasets generated by our products and turn raw data into meaningful signals, insights, and features.

You will work across the entire data lifecycle: building reliable pipelines, exploring and understanding complex datasets, developing features from them, and creating the tools and visualizations needed to understand their quality and impact.

This is a technical and product-oriented data role. You'll collaborate closely with product, engineering, and data teams to find what we can learn from our data and turn those learnings into production systems.

As a Data Engineer, your day-to-day will include:

  • Making Sense of Data

    • Explore large and complex datasets to understand user behavior and identify useful patterns and signals.

    • Transform raw data into reliable, well-defined features that can be used by our products and engineering teams.

    • Develop a deep understanding of our data: where it comes from, what it represents, its limitations, and how it can be combined to answer new questions.

  • Building Data Products

    • Design, build, and maintain pipelines that process large volumes of data efficiently and reliably.

    • Take ideas from exploration to production: prototype them on historical data, evaluate their quality, and build the pipelines needed to run them at scale.

    • Build datasets and features that can power product experiences, internal systems, analytics, and machine learning models.

    • Work with technologies such as Spark, DBT, Dagster, BigQuery, ClickHouse, DuckDB, or similar tools depending on the problem at hand.

  • Exploring & Analyzing

    • Use data to investigate hypotheses, understand behaviors, and answer ambiguous questions.

    • Develop metrics and evaluation frameworks to understand whether the signals and features we build actually work.

    • Create analyses, dashboards, and visualizations that make complex datasets understandable and help the team make better decisions.

    • Build tooling that makes it easier to inspect individual examples, debug data pipelines, and understand why a system produces a particular result.

  • From Data to Intelligence

    • Work closely with engineers and product teams to identify opportunities where data can make our products smarter.

    • Use statistical methods, heuristics, experimentation, or machine learning depending on what is most appropriate for the problem.

    • Iterate on features and models based on real-world data and continuously improve their accuracy and reliability.

    • Help bridge the gap between exploratory data work and robust systems running in production.

  • Continuous Improvement

    • Improve the performance, reliability, and maintainability of our data infrastructure.

    • Monitor data quality and proactively investigate unexpected changes or anomalies.

    • Stay up to date with developments in data engineering, analytics, and machine learning, and bring relevant ideas and technologies into our stack.

    • Contribute to a culture of curiosity, craftsmanship, and learning.

Your Skills & Experience

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals and experience working with data-intensive systems.

  • Very comfortable with SQL and manipulating large datasets.

  • Experience with one or more modern data technologies such as Spark, DBT, Dagster, BigQuery, ClickHouse, DuckDB, or equivalent tools.

  • Strong analytical skills: you enjoy digging into data, testing hypotheses, and understanding why something behaves the way it does.

  • Ability to turn exploratory analysis into reliable, production-ready data pipelines and features.

  • Familiarity with data modeling, pipeline orchestration, and large-scale data processing.

  • Ability to communicate findings clearly through metrics, visualizations, dashboards, or other tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building data products or features directly used by consumer-facing products.

  • Experience working with high-volume event, behavioral, sensor, geospatial, or time-series data.

  • Familiarity with statistics, machine learning, or feature engineering.

  • Experience taking a data problem from an ambiguous question through exploration, prototyping, evaluation, and production.

Our Stack

About Linkup
Our Vision

We believe in a future of AI agents and the agentic web. These digital entities can create more value for humanity than we ever could alone, but they depend on the internet to operate, collaborate, take action, and gather information.

AI agents need web search. To perform well, they require information that is current, reliable, and context‑specific—not the diffuse, steadily aging knowledge frozen at their last training cut‑off.

Modern web search is built for humans, not AIs. Instead of trusted facts, it serves links, ads, and click‑bait. People want visually engaging pages; AI systems need structured truth. An AI can absorb oceans of data, while human attention barely skims the surface. Humans think visually and intuitively; AI reasons in latent space.

Web 2.0 is sunsetting. The deck is being reshuffled, and the Bing‑Google search oligopoly is crumbling. Indexing ever more pages is no longer the goal; semantically organizing facts for AI systems is. In the coming agentic web, Google’s ad‑driven model has no natural home.

Search for AI must be rebuilt from the ground up. We are reconstructing the web as a rigorously structured knowledge layer, mapping every concept, entity, and claim into a coherent semantic graph. This foundation delivers verified facts and rich context to AI instantly, unlocking faster reasoning, higher accuracy, and radically more useful answers for everyone.

Humans search Google; AI searches Linkup.

 

Our Mission

Reality never stands still, and neither should intelligence. Linkup reconnects language models to a living stream of verified facts, ensuring AIs remain as current and insightful as the world they serve.

Our mission is to deliver the world’s freshest, most trusted knowledge to AIs.

 

Our Culture

Our culture is built on the following values:

  • Mission. We believe we play a critical role in building the agentic web. We are 100% committed to our mission of bringing the reality of the world to AI agents.

  • Speed. We build fast, we build to last. We get things done, well.

  • Ownership. We empower every team member to take ownership of their projects, ensuring they see them through to successful completion.

  • Teamwork. Our strength lies in our unity. We rely on one another and embrace our diversity as a core asset.

  • Humility. We maintain low egos, showing respect for others and continuously learning from their insights and experiences.

We expect all team member to take an active role in shaping our company culture.

Bleu Robotics is an AI company developing universal AI software for the deployment of advanced robots , humanoids, mobile manipulators, and industrial arms, in real factories. The convergence of humanoid robotics and modern AI is one of the most significant technical opportunities of the decade, and most of the work today still happens in research settings. We have a strong ambition to become the next Microsoft to run on every industrial humanoid. We have closed our pre-seed round with Top-tier fund to deploy our robot in Tier 1 manufacturing facilities.

Our vision

To enable a robot to learn a new industrial task from a few demonstrations and operate autonomously, with under one hour between the start of the demonstration and the start of deployment.

This objective shapes our roadmap and every technical decision we make.

The role

We are hiring Research Scientists in Vision & Perception to design the perception stack that makes our robots understand their environment well enough to act in it reliably. Your work will define how our robots see the world, what they recognize, how robustly, and from how little data.

Industrial environments are visually complex, varied, and unforgiving: changing lighting, cluttered scenes, novel objects, and a hard requirement to work in production without supervision. The perception layer has to deliver the spatial and semantic understanding required for learned manipulation policies to succeed, across the many tasks, objects, and sites we will deploy on. Hitting our one-hour demonstration-to-deployment target depends directly on perception methods that work robustly out of the box, with minimal site-specific tuning.

This is a research role focused on shipping algorithms into a real product. We are an early-stage company and do not publish at this stage. You will work in close collaboration with the Robot Learning and Integration teams to ensure the methods you develop run on real robots, in real factories.

Responsibilities

  • Design, prototype, and evaluate perception algorithms for robotic manipulation — object recognition, segmentation, pose estimation, scene understanding, and related areas

  • Advance our internal state of the art in perception for embodied agents, with a focus on robustness and data efficiency

  • Run rigorous experiments on real robots, and contribute to the data, evaluation, and infrastructure needed to do so (we will support you in ramping up on robotics if your background is primarily in vision)

  • Translate research prototypes into perception components robust enough to ship as part of our product

  • Collaborate with the Robot Learning and Integration teams to move research from prototype to production

  • Help shape the long-term research agenda of the company

The team

The engineering team is organized around three focus areas with multiple contributors each: Integration, Vision & Perception (this role), and Robot Learning. Early hires will help shape the research agenda, engineering practices, hiring, and culture.

Required qualifications

  • PhD or MSc in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, or a closely related field, from a leading research lab or strong experience in research environments

  • Track record of published research at top venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICML, ICRA, IROS, CoRL, RSS, or equivalent

  • Demonstrated research expertise in computer vision or machine perception — object recognition, segmentation, pose estimation, scene understanding, 3D perception, or representation learning for vision

  • Strong Python skills and fluency with PyTorch

  • Hands-on experience training, evaluating, and debugging modern vision systems

  • Professional proficiency in English (internal working language)

Preferred qualifications

The strongest candidates will combine deep research expertise with experience across several of the following:

  • 3D vision — depth estimation, geometric reasoning, point cloud processing, or 3D scene reconstruction

  • Perception for robotic manipulation, including grasping and interaction

  • Experience working with real robots (any platform — humanoids, arms, mobile bases)

  • Postdoctoral experience, or research positions in industry labs or top academic groups

  • A history of translating research into deployed systems

What we offer

  • A diverse fleet of advanced robots, including humanoids, on which to run your research

  • Research that ships: your algorithms run on real machines in real factories

  • Tight collaboration with engineering teams that take your work to production

description:
Part-Time | Switzerland (Remote) | Global EOR & HR Platform | Employed via Swiss Entity

Our client is a fast-growing global HR, payroll, and compliance platform operating across 180+ regions. We are looking for an HR & EOR Operations Manager to join our Swiss entity on a part-time basis. This is a hands-on operational role - not a purely administrative or advisory position.

As part of the role, you will serve as the named Responsible Person for the Swiss entity under SECO/Zürich personnel leasing law, fulfilling a standing legal obligation tied to our EOR licence. Day-to-day workload is manageable within a 50% FTE, and you will be fully supported by the company's global HR, payroll and compliance teams. Other concurrent work or mandates are welcome, provided they do not interfere with your availability and supervision of the entity's activities.

This role is a strong fit for HR or EOR professionals already freelancing, holding consulting mandates, or looking to add a substantive part-time role to their portfolio.

  • Act as the named Responsible Person for the Swiss entity under Swiss personnel leasing (SECO) law.

  • Ensure compliance with Swiss labour-leasing legislation, Swiss employment law, and the staffing industry GAV (minimum wages and equal treatment).

  • Maintain documentation required for SECO and cantonal audits and inspections.

  • Serve as the primary Swiss contact for SECO and cantonal authorities.

  • Oversee HR and employment operations for the Swiss entity - including onboarding, contract controls, and employment matters.

  • Support payroll oversight in collaboration with the global payroll team.

  • Handle employee and client escalations related to HR and compliance matters.

  • Supervise the entity's EOR/personnel leasing activities and ensure they are conducted properly.

Right to Work in Switzerland - one of the following is required:

  • Swiss citizen.

  • EU/EFTA national with a current Swiss B or C permit.

  • Non-EU/EFTA national with a Swiss C permit (a non-EU/EFTA B permit alone does not qualify).

  • EU/EFTA national with a genuine 5-year cross-border G permit.

Education:

Any completed qualification - EFZ apprenticeship, Matura/Abitur, or university degree in any field.

Standard route:

3+ years in one of the following: recruitment or placement, personnel leasing or staffing (including EOR), substantive HR (not admin-only), personnel consulting, or organisational/business consulting. Employment certificates confirming dates, workload percentage and substantive duties are required alongside a CV.

Alternative route:

3+ years of general professional experience plus a completed, recognised HR qualification with a passed exam (e.g. HRSE or VSH HR Assistant). Course attendance without a final certificate does not count.

Character:

Clean criminal record, debt-enforcement register and tax history.

description:
Mobileye is looking for a passionate Systems Software Developer to join the Operating System Team in the
EyeQ Platform Software Group. While many work on Linux, we work in Linux. Our team is responsible for the
core OS DNA of the EyeQ computer vision SoC, defining how the system starts, is composed, and manages its
lifecycle in a high-performance automotive environment.

We are looking for an experienced systems engineer to join our Core Distribution team. The center of this role
is the Linux userspace and the distribution itself: boot and service bring-up, root filesystem composition, and
the integration of external SDK into that platform. You will also build Python-based deployment tooling so the
OS and SDK stack can be provisioned reproducibly - infrastructure and tool development in service of the OS.


What will your job look like
  • Architect and develop Linux userspace and service bring-up so the distribution boots into a consistent,
    operational platform under embedded constraints.
  • Enable and integrate an SDK into the OS image - drivers, libraries, runtimes, and filesystem layout as
    first-class distribution components.
  • Own distribution composition, including packages, sysroots, and image features that make the SDK and
    core OS a maintainable, versioned platform.
  • Develop Python-based deployment tooling to provision targets with a reproducible OS + SDK environment
    (image delivery, flashing, and environment setup).
  • Debug at the OS boundary - init/service failures, library and ABI mismatches, missing dependencies, and
    SDK/runtime issues on the target.
  • Perform root cause analysis on system-level failures in the distribution, from boot and userspace bring-up
    through a fully operational stack.
  • Collaborate on board bring-up, tailoring the distribution and SDK integration to new EyeQ generations and
    related target hardware.

    • All you need is:
  • Outstanding graduate in Computer Science or similar field.  
  • 5+ years of experience in Embedded Linux development, with a focus on systems software, userspace, or
    distribution work.
  • Strong C/C++ skills and a solid understanding of POSIX APIs, libraries, and how userspace talks to the
    kernel.
  • Deep knowledge of Linux Internals, specifically the boot process (Bootloaders, Kernel hand-off, Init
    systems) and root filesystem layout.
  • Hands-on experience with Embedded Linux Distributions (e.g., custom Yocto recipes, Buildroot, or
    Linux-from-scratch).
  • Experience enabling vendor SDKs or BSP stacks on Linux — integrating third-party drivers, runtimes, and
    userspace components into a custom image.
  • Proficiency in debugging tools like GDB, Valgrind, strace, and perf.
  • Experience with Python for infrastructure and tool development — deployment, packaging, and
    environment setup.

    • Nice to have:
  • Background in Automotive Software .\
  • Experience with GPU/accelerator compute stacks (driver + userspace runtime, inference/compute
    libraries, cross-sysroot workflows).
  • Familiarity with reading hardware schematics and reasoning about basic hardware interfaces and signal.

title: Product Manager (f/m/d)
description:
Description

We are seeking a product manager to own the "what" and "why" of our quantum sensing measurement systems. You turn customer and market needs into clear product requirements that engineering can turn into specifications, and you own the roadmap for the QDm product line, starting with QDm.1. You sit between our customers (foundries, IDMs, OSATs and failure analysis labs) and every engineering discipline, and you make sure we build the right product in the right order.


Who we are

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.


Why join us?

Picture this:

  • Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.
  • Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.
  • Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.
  • An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.
Still unsure about why joining us?
  • You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.
  • From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.
  • Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.
  • You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.
Let’s make the invisible visible!


What will you do

  • Own the product requirements: gather needs from customers, the field, the market, and internal stakeholders (serviceability, modularity and product configuration, manufacturability, and cost targets), and turn them into clear, prioritized, solution-neutral requirements.
  • Establish our requirements engineering tooling and workflow: select and set up how we capture, trace, and maintain requirements, from customer need through specification to verification, including change control across releases. This is a foundational task in your first months.
  • Own and maintain the QDm.1 roadmap: propose what gets built and in what order, make the trade-offs explicit, and align decisions with the management team.
  • Work with the applications team on customer interactions and evaluations with fabs, IDMs, OSATs and failure analysis labs, and translate what you learn into requirements.
  • For each requirement, define acceptance criteria from the customer's point of view so it is clear and testable when the need is met, and link them to customer evaluation and qualification plans.
  • Align with the Product Development department on scope and timing, and hand solution-neutral requirements into engineering: state the need and the why, and leave the how to the disciplines.
  • Support go-to-market: give input on positioning, pricing, launch readiness, and documentation scope together with the applications, operations, and product development teams.


What is expected of you

  • Several years in product management for complex hardware or capital equipment, ideally in semiconductor, metrology, or a comparable deep-tech environment.
  • A track record of writing clear product requirements that engineering can actually build from.
  • The ability to talk to both customers and engineers and to translate between them.
  • Enough technical depth to hold a credible conversation with the people designing the product, across mechanics, optics, electronics/RF, and software.
  • Structured prioritization: you make trade-offs explicit and back them with reasoning.
  • We hire for demonstrated skill rather than a specific degree; a technical or scientific background is typical. The working language is English.
Additional experience we value:
  • Semiconductor industry knowledge (fabs, IDMs, OSATs, inspection, metrology, or failure analysis).
  • Familiarity with SEMI standards and fab tool integration (for example, S2/S8, E10, SECS/GEM).
  • Experience selecting or setting up a requirements management tool (for example, Jama, Polarion, or CodeBeamer).
  • A working understanding of quantum sensing, optics, or precision instrumentation.


Our benefits

  • Mission: At QD, we’re driven by more than just building great products - we aim to make a lasting difference. Joining us means contributing to meaningful work that goes beyond business as usual.
  • Impact & growth: This is an exciting stage of our journey, and your voice matters. You’ll have the chance to shape our culture, influence key decisions, and grow alongside a company that’s scaling fast.
  • Health & fitness: With a company-sponsored Wellpass membership, you’ll have access to countless gyms, classes, and wellness offers across Germany to stay healthy and active.
  • Team & culture: We believe the best ideas come when we connect outside the office. From regular off-sites to team events, you’ll be part of a collaborative and supportive environment.
  • Well-being & balance: We value rest and recovery. That’s why you’ll enjoy 30 vacation days plus public holidays to recharge and return inspired.
  • Learning & development: Your growth is our priority. We provide an annual budget dedicated to courses, conferences, or any resources that help you expand your skills.
  • Ownership & participation: As part of our equity program, you’ll directly share in our success and the value we create together.

  • Erfahrung mit verteilten Systemen, Gerätedaten, Messaging oder technischen Schnittstellen

  • Vertrautheit mit CI/CD, Observability oder Platform Engineering

title: Senior Software Engineer (m/f/x)
description:
About us

The appliedAI Initiative elevates Europe’s industry to become shapers in the age of AI, creating a future that we desire to live in. Through our ecosystem of strong partners, comprehensive programs, services and solutions we advance companies holistically on their AI journey. With our uniquely diverse, interdisciplinary, and driven team, we build on deep technical expertise while specializing on applicability of the solutions. We share a mindset of collaboration and openness with our ecosystem of leading companies and tech players. Our common goal is to strengthen the European landscape, jointly creating unique knowledge for applying trustworthy AI. We believe that AI Agents will be the dominant topic for AI in the near future and that appliedAI with its partner ecosystem will impact how this technology is being used in industry and beyond in Europe.


Your mission

Most of what makes an AI solution survive contact with a large enterprise is not the AI. It is the engineering discipline around it, and that discipline is what you bring. You do not need to arrive as an AI expert - you arrive as someone who knows how professional software gets built, shipped, and kept alive, and you grow into the agentic side alongside a team that is already deep in it. In our Engineering team you set the bar for what production-ready means here.
Your tasks will include:

  • Designing the technical approach for a system slice, from build and test through deployment and operation, including the documentation and artefacts a third party needs to run it without us
  • Shaping how we develop: issue workflows, branching and review standards, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, security checks, and release management
  • Building the classical software around the AI core - services and APIs, data pipelines, infrastructure as code, mostly in Python on Azure 
  • Making solutions operable in enterprise IT landscapes: observability, failure behaviour, security posture, and cost transparency
  • Providing specialist guidance that shapes technical decisions across workstreams, and raising the engineering bar through design and code reviews
  • Making technical trade-offs legible to senior client stakeholders - what a given architecture or operating model costs and enables


Your profile

  • 8+ years building software that went into production and stayed there, ideally shaped by a product organisation with real release discipline
  • Deep working knowledge of the professional software development lifecycle: issue tracking and workflows (e.g. Jira), code review and development standards, CI/CD, automated testing, security scanning, versioning and releases
  • Strong Python, confidence on Azure, and hands-on experience with containers and infrastructure as code
  • Experience handing a system over to a separate operating team, or having operated one yourself long enough to know what that handover really demands
  • Some exposure to GenAI or agentic systems and genuine curiosity to go deeper; deep AI expertise is explicitly not a prerequisite
  • Composure in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, and the ability to explain technical trade-offs clearly to senior stakeholders in English; German is a plus


What we offer

  • A highly qualified and motivated team of ~90 people is on a journey to change the rapidly evolving European AI Landscape
  • Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work model: You can choose to work from our vibrant offices - either at the IPAI in Heilbronn or the House of Communication in Munich - while also enjoying the flexibility to work remotely a few days each week
  • Opportunity to shape a variety of projects and the development of new, original content based on the latest developments in AI and its adoption in businesses
  • An atmosphere that encourages to think and experiment in new ways with software, hardware, and processes
  • A highly visible initiative that helps you build a large and high-level network of start-ups, partners, and tech companies
  • A flexible development budget that’s yours to shape - invest it in training, certifications, conferences, or new challenges, however you want to grow
  • Sports membership with Wellpass to access thousands of sports facilities all over Germany (and beyond), as well as online courses

title: Head of Supply Chain (f/m/d) - Berlin
description:
About us

At CYCLE, we're redefining urban mobility for the people who keep cities moving: couriers, riders, and delivery pros. Our e-bike subscription service combines durable vehicles, fast repairs, and real support, everything riders need to stay on the road.
From Berlin to London, Vienna to Amsterdam, we operate in 200+ cities across Europe, providing thousands of riders with bikes built for work, not for show.
Our mission is simple: make last-mile delivery more reliable, affordable, and sustainable, one ride at a time. With every bike we deploy, we're helping build the backbone of smarter, greener cities.
Ride with us into the future - sustainable, efficient, and full speed ahead!


Your Mission

As Head of Supply Chain, you own every part of how physical goods reach our fleet and our riders, from the purchase order to the shelf to the courier's bike. You report to our Director of Operations and work directly with Hardware, Finance, Software and our country teams. In particular you will:

  • Own supply chain end to end: Purchasing, warehousing, stock keeping and outbound logistics across our European network, as one function with one owner. You ultimately ensure we have the right number of bikes, batteries and parts at the right time, the right place and the best price.
  • Oversee our assembly & refurbishment activities: Manage our assembly and refurbishment partners, own the bills of material for everything we build from purchased components as well as internal refurbishment within our locations.
  • Own the systems, not just the process: Take full responsibility for our ERP and warehouse management setup for all supply chain topics, from data model and master data through to daily execution – you will be the business owner to our software team and guide implementation.
  • Professionalize the structure: Design and implement the processes, controls and physical setup our growing operation needs, and then get your hands dirty making them real and ensuring your organization internalizes them.
  • Own the numbers behind the goods: You will guide the rest of the company on such topics as transfer prices, landed cost allocation and other supply-chain related financials, ensuring each business line's P&L is accurately reflecting parts consumption and asset usage – together with our Finance team.
  • Drive the agenda across teams: Set priorities, align Hardware, Finance and Tech behind them, and hold the line when it matters. 
  • Partner with the larger organization and understand your impact on them: All you do, you do with the end goal in mind to become the best friend of our Local and Country Operations and Sales teams, who all depend on your fulfillment excellence to grow and maintain their businesses.
  • Lead and grow your team: Build a supply chain organization that scales with us across markets.


Your skills and qualifications

We are looking for someone who has built structure inside a well-run company and is ready to build it again from scratch, with their sleeves rolled up. Ideally you bring:

  • 10+ years of relevant professional experience, of which at least 5 in a managerial supply chain or operations role.
  • Experience leading a team of at least 3 direct reports in a supply chain or operations-heavy function.
  • Structure from an established company: You have worked inside proper processes and systems and know what good looks like.
  • 0 to 1 experience: You have also built something from nothing in a smaller or fast-moving company or demonstrated you can excel in such a setting, and you are comfortable being scrappy when that is what the situation needs.
  • Commercial and financial fluency: Working capital optimization, inter-company transactions or product costing,  are all familiar territory for you.
  • Cross-functional communication: You can carry a topic across teams and drive it to a decision.
  • Ownership and a firm, professional attitude: You take the whole problem, not your part of it.
  • English at C1 level or above

Nice to have:
  • Hands-on experience with Odoo or a comparable ERP, ideally including experience in shaping or designing a system for supply chain topics rather than execution alone.
  • Background in bike, scooter, mobility or another hardware-heavy industry where physical goods move between internal as well as external locations.
  • German or Dutch


What you can expect from us


  • Exciting industry: You will work in the dynamic world of mobility, which is a constantly evolving sector.
  • Real impact: Your work improves the lives of many bike couriers.
  • Take on immediate responsibility: Start making a difference right away and implement your own ideas. Boredom? Not a chance!
  • Shape the future: As part of our growing start-up, you will help to shape tomorrow's mobility.
  • International team & Strong network: Work alongside motivated colleagues from all over the world. Teamwork is very important to us.
  • Fair conditions: We offer a stable employment with attractive salary, €50 HRmony voucher, a company e-bike, modern equipment and 28 days' holiday a year.


Diversity

At CYCLE, we believe diversity makes us stronger. No matter who you are, where you're from, or what makes you unique, you're welcome here.

lemon.markets is a Brokerage-as-a-Service platform: simple digital access to capital markets through a single API. As our ICT Outsourcing Manager, you strengthen how lemon.markets manages and governs external technology services, outsourcing arrangements, and third-party risk in a regulated environment. Sitting at the intersection of Technology, Compliance, Operations, and partner governance, this role helps ensure that our provider landscape is transparent, well-documented, risk-based, and operationally under control. You will help turn recurring governance work into reliable operating routines, from assessments and reporting to escalations and evidence gathering. This is a hands-on role with real impact, especially for someone who enjoys creating structure, driving follow-up, and continuously improving operational processes.

In this role you will:

  • Act as the first line competence centre for ICT outsourcing and third-party governance topics, working across Technology, Compliance, Operations, business owners, and external partners to ensure risks and responsibilities are transparent and well managed.

  • Have enough technical affinity to understand IT services, security-related topics, incidents, and operational dependencies without needing to be a security engineer.

  • Work in a highly structured and reliable way, with strong follow-up discipline, good judgment, and the ability to keep multiple stakeholders aligned.

WHY US?

title: Health claims lead (f/m/x)
description:
Intro

As our Health Claims lead, you'll own claims decisions on Feather's health MGA books from day one: coverage, declines, settlement amounts, all within policy terms. You'll manage our insurance carrier relationships, decide how we work with service providers, and build the playbook, automations and systems that let the function scale as we grow MGA health claims fast across expat and international health.

At Feather, we're building insurance that actually matters to our customers. It rests on three principles: a fully digital experience, modern and flexible plans, and reliable human support. And because we build it all for expats living abroad, we're a genuinely different kind of insurer.


Why work at Feather?

  • We're small, lean, and we love what we do. The usual buzzwords here, except we actually mean them. Staying small helps us focus on what matters, and we want to keep it that way.
  • You'll work on a product that is loved by customers. Our excellent Trustpilot and Google reviews speak for themselves.
  • There's plenty of space to grow. We trust you to take ownership and make real decisions from day one, and you'll have all the support you need to succeed.
  • You'll have the freedom to build something from scratch. You're not inheriting a finished system. You're building the decision logic, reporting, and playbook that let health claims scale.
  • Flexible remote work policy. We offer a remote-first work environment, hiring across Europe via an Employer of Record. We host company retreats, team dinners, and meetups to spend in-person time together.


What you bring to the table

  • You have hands-on experience handling health claims across borders or internationally.
  • You are familiar with medical coding and provider billing.
  • You have an instinct for automation and AI tooling, and you use it daily.
  • You take tough decisions daily, including saying no to customers, and you still enjoy the work.
  • You are pragmatic in an unfinished system: you improve it while running it.
  • You are a fluent English speaker.
Nice to have:
  • German, Spanish, or French language skills.
  • Experience with moratorium underwriting.
  • A medical background.
  • Experience in an MGA or delegated authority setup.
  • Experience managing third-party administrators (TPAs).


You'll be responsible for

  • You will make claims decisions
    • You will interpret coverage, decide declines, settlement amounts, and goodwill within policy terms, with real authority, not recommend-and-wait.
    • You will handle expat and international health claims: cross-border invoices across languages and billing conventions, currency and tax, and coordination with statutory and private cover in the country of residence.
  • You will manage our carrier relationships
    • You will own claims reporting and bordereaux, contentious cases, and coverage disputes with our insurance partners.
    • You will keep audit-ready records throughout, so nothing surprises the carrier.
  • You will decide how we work with service providers
    • You will decide where using third-party administrators (TPAs) makes sense, and manage instructions, quality, turnaround, and commercial performance where we use them.
  • You will build the operating model
    • You will close gaps with product and engineering across intake, documents, decision support, payout, and automation.
    • You will run audits and fraud checks, working toward semi-automated monitoring with the data team.
  • You will build capability
    • You will write the playbook so health claims stops depending on one person.
    • You will train whoever joins the team next.


What will the interview process look like?

  1. CV screening
  2. Initial phone call with our People team. We'll have a chat and get to know each other (30m)
  3. Hiring manager call. We'll cover the role, skills needed, and answer your questions (1 hour)
  4. Case study. We'll give you a case study to work on, which will give you an idea of the type of projects you'd take on at Feather (3-4h)
  5. Case study discussion. We'll go through your reasoning and approach together (90min)
  6. Call with our Head of Ops. We'll talk through our async, remote-first way of working and how our team operates day to day (45min)
  7. Final interview. You'll be speaking to one member of our leadership team (45min)


Does this sound like a good fit for you? Apply now!

At Feather, we actively foster inclusive representation within our teams and embrace a diverse mix of talent. We encourage applicants from all educational paths to apply: we believe that what you’ve built, worked on, and achieved is far more important than on-paper qualifications.

title: Working Student Modeled Data
description:
At Statista, we’re all about facts and data, for we are the world's leading business data platform. By providing reliable and easy-to-use data as well as various data analytics products and services, we empower people worldwide to make fact-based decisions.

Founded in Hamburg in 2007, we have quickly grown into a global company with offices in major cities such as London, New York, Berlin and Tokyo. And we still have a lot of plans. Our constant growth does not only prove our success, but also keeps creating new development and career opportunities for our employees.

We value and celebrate our diverse culture. You are welcome here for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or whether you prefer bar graphs to pie charts. Your story matters – keep writing it as part of our team.

Are you ready to join us?

Our Mission

As AI rapidly transforms how information is created and consumed, high-quality proprietary data is becoming the critical ingredient for generating trustworthy insights and enabling better decisions. Models become more powerful as the quality of the underlying data improves.

The mission of the Modeled Data department is to develop high-quality proprietary data at scale, empowering our customers to make better business decisions with confidence.

To achieve this, we are building the next generation of proprietary data production: a standardized, AI-enabled production system that combines artificial intelligence and human expertise to deliver scalable, transparent, and high-quality outputs.

We believe the future is not AI instead of analysts, but AI together with analysts. AI excels at automating repetitive work, scaling production, and accelerating execution, while analysts contribute structured problem solving, statistical reasoning, domain expertise, and critical judgment. Together, they create outcomes that neither could achieve alone.

Our analysts therefore have a dual mission: they continuously deepen their expertise in business domains and statistical modeling while simultaneously helping build and improve the AI-powered production platform that will define the future of proprietary data.

 
 

Your Role

As a Working Student, you will support our analysts in building and maintaining proprietary data and contribute to improving our analytical workflows and production systems.

 

Your responsibilities

  • Support the analysis of structured and unstructured data from internal and external sources

  • Assist in collecting, cleaning, and preparing datasets for modeling and analysis

  • Help build and maintain Python-based analytical workflows and scripts

  • Support analysts in identifying trends, patterns, and key market insights

  • Assist in improving data pipelines, methodologies, and documentation

  • Contribute to ongoing projects that aim to make our data production more scalable and efficient

 
 

Your Profile

  • Enrolled student at a university (mandatory)

  • Field of study in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, or a related quantitative discipline (preferred)

  • Strong analytical thinking and structured problem-solving skills

  • Basic experience with Python (e.g., through coursework, projects, or internships)

  • Interest in data, markets, and business dynamics

  • Ability to work independently and in a structured way

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills (English required, German is a plus)

 

Nice to have

  • Experience with SQL or databases

  • Familiarity with data analysis or visualization tools

  • Exposure to statistical methods or market research

  • Interest in AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Copilot)

 
 

Your Team

You will be part of an international, data-driven team working on analytical projects across different markets and industries. You will support real modeling and data production work while gaining hands-on experience with data, tools, and methodologies.

 

This role offers the opportunity to learn how proprietary data is built at scale and how analytical workflows can be combined with AI to create scalable data products.

What we offer

In addition to our great team, culture, and our shared goal of empowering people with data, there are many other things that make Statista a great place to work! Join us and benefit from:

  • Work from abroad up to 30 calendar days a year

  • Hybrid work and flex-time

  • Subsidized urban mobility and access to fitness and wellness options

  • Free access to Langdock and all its amazing functionalities

  • Career & training opportunities
