title: Professional Backend Developer (w/m/d)
description:
Wer Du bist

Du hast 3-5 Jahre Erfahrung im Java-Stack und beherrschst Spring Boot souverän. Du entwickelst komplexe Features eigenständig von der Konzeption bis zum Release, denkst analytisch und trägst aktiv zu Architekturentscheidungen bei. Du nutzt KI-Assistenz (z.B. GitHub Copilot, Cursor, ChatGPT) als etabliertes Produktivitätswerkzeug – nicht nur zum Code-Generieren, sondern auch für komplexe Refactorings, Architektur-Diskussionen und Debugging – übernimmst aber die volle Verantwortung für Qualität, Security und Nachvollziehbarkeit der Lösungen. Du arbeitest selbstorganisiert, kommunizierst auf Augenhöhe mit Stakeholdern und unterstützt gern weniger erfahrene Entwickler beim Wachsen.

Wer wir sind

Plunet GmbH mit Standorten in Berlin, Würzburg und New York entwickelt und vertreibt die Business- und Workflow-Management-Software „Plunet BusinessManager“ – eine der weltweit führenden Managementlösungen für die Übersetzungs- und Lokalisierungsbranche. Unsere Kunden sind führende Übersetzungsagenturen, Regierungsorganisationen und NGOs sowie große internationale Industrie- und Dienstleistungsunternehmen.

Aufgaben

  • Entwicklung & Architektur: Du entwirfst und implementierst komplexe, skalierbare Backend-Lösungen mit Spring Boot, inkl. Konfiguration von Security-Mechanismen und Integration von Drittbibliotheken. Du hilfst mit, technische Lösungen in unserer Software-Architektur zu gestalten.
  • Qualitätssicherung: Du führst Code Reviews durch und stellst umfassende Testabdeckung mit JUnit, Mockito und SpringBootTest sicher – inkl. komplexer Integrationstests
  • Legacy & Modernisierung: Du refactorst bestehenden Code und modernisierst Kernkomponenten (Main Classes), ohne dabei die Systemstabilität zu gefährden.
  • Datenbanken: Du optimierst Datenbankabfragen und -designs (MySQL/MSSQL) und setzt Hibernate als ORM-Werkzeug für komplexe Mapping-Szenarien fortgeschritten ein.
  • Wissenstransfer: Du bist aktives Mitglied in unseren Communities of Practice (CoPs), leitest diese bei Bedarf und mentorst Junior-Entwickler bei Onboarding und fachlicher Entwicklung.
  • Integration: Du integrierst den Plunet BusinessManager mit externen Systemen und arbeitest eng mit Product Specialists zusammen.
  • KI-Integration: Du nutzt KI-Tools effektiv für Entwicklungstasks, validierst generierten Code kritisch hinsichtlich Clean Code, Security und Performance und hilfst mit, Best Practices für den KI-Einsatz im Team zu etablieren.

Qualifikation

  • Erfahrung: 3-5 Jahre professionelle Softwareentwicklung mit Schwerpunkt Backend/Java.
  • Java Advanced: Fortgeschrittene Kenntnisse von Design Patterns, Multithreading, Concurrency und aktuellen Java-Versionen.
  • Spring Boot: Erfahrung in der Entwicklung komplexer, skalierbarer Anwendungen; sicherer Umgang mit Security-Konfiguration und externer API-Integration.
  • Softwaretests: Advanced-Level in Unit- und Integrationstests mit JUnit, Mockito und SpringBootTest; Erfahrung mit Testautomatisierung.
  • Datenbanken: Fortgeschrittene SQL-Kenntnisse (MySQL, MSSQL), Query-Optimierung und sicherer Umgang mit Hibernate.
  • Tooling: Sicherer Umgang mit Git, CI/CD-Pipelines und modernen IDEs (IntelliJ, VSCode).
  • KI-Assistenz Professional: Erfahrener Umgang mit KI-Coding-Assistenz für komplexe Entwicklungsszenarien; Fähigkeit zum effektiven Prompt Engineering; kritische Bewertung von KI-Vorschlägen hinsichtlich Architektur-Patterns, Security-Risiken und Datenschutz; Bewusstsein für Limitationen und Halluzinationen.
  • Clean Code: Du lebst Clean Code-Prinzipien aktiv und hilfst anderen dabei, besser zu werden.
  • Soft Skills: Starke analytische Fähigkeit zur Analyse komplexer Anforderungen und Entwurf effizienter Lösungen; hervorragende Selbstorganisation (Priorisierung, Zeitmanagement); exzellente Kommunikations- und Teamfähigkeit zur Zusammenarbeit mit Architekten und Stakeholdern; Bereitschaft, Junior-Entwickler zu mentoren und Wissen weiterzugeben.
  • Sprachen: Sehr gute Englischkenntnisse (B2+), Deutsch ist ein Plus.

Nice-to-haves (Zusätzliche Aktivitäten & Skills)

  • Security: Erfahrung mit der Analyse und Behebung von Sicherheitslücken in Dependencies (OWASP Dependency-Check, Sicherheitsmanagement).
  • DevOps/Tooling: Kenntnisse in Liquibase, SonarQube, GitLab Administration oder Docker.
  • Performance: Erfahrung mit Performance-Analyse (Thread-Dumps, Heap-Dumps) und Last-tests.
  • Fullstack-Perspektive: Grundkenntnisse in Angular, TypeScript oder .NET.
  • Methodik: Erfahrung mit agilen Frameworks (Scrum/Kanban) als aktiver Teamplayer.
  • Schulung: Du erstellst Präsentationen und Schulungen für andere Entwickler, um spezifisches Wissen zu verbreiten.

Benefits

Warum Plunet? Bei uns stehen die Menschen im Mittelpunkt

  • Unabhängig & menschenorientiert: Plunet ist ein inhabergeführtes Unternehmen ohne Investoren – deshalb können wir uns wirklich um jede und jeden Einzelnen kümmern. Wir fördern transparente Kommunikation und respektvolle Zusammenarbeit und geben allen eine Stimme.
  • Work-Life-Balance: Genieße ein flexibles Arbeitsumfeld, in dem Dein Wohlbefinden an erster Stelle steht. Profitiere von flexiblen Arbeitszeiten, fairen Überstundenregelungen und der Möglichkeit, 4 Wochen im Jahr remote zu arbeiten.
  • Nachhaltig unterwegs: Fahre ein Dienstrad (auch E-Bikes!) und nutze die steuerlichen Vorteile. Außerdem bezuschussen wir das Deutschlandticket.
  • Gemeinsame Momente & gutes Essen: Wir kochen regelmäßig gemeinsam zu Mittag und frühstücken zusammen. Genieße Deine Mahlzeiten mit Kolleginnen und Kollegen in unseren schön eingerichteten Büros in Berlin, Würzburg und New York. Unsere gut ausgestatteten Küchen laden zum gemeinsamen Kochen und Essen ein, und wir bieten einen Essenszuschuss (Profit von Hrmony). Und: WIR LIEBEN unsere frischen Obstkörbe :-D
  • Eigenverantwortung & Agilität: Dich erwartet ein hohes Maß an Eigenverantwortung und Gestaltungsfreiheit. Wir arbeiten agil und transparent und wollen unsere Ziele nachhaltig erreichen. Deshalb setzen wir auf flache Hierarchien und wenig Bürokratie.
  • Plunet-Teamgeist: Wir leben den Plunet-Teamgeist: einen offenen, respektvollen Umgang miteinander über alle Rollen hinweg.
  • Entwicklung & Wirkung: Werde Teil eines wunderbaren Teams, in dem wir aufeinander achten und gemeinsam die Marktführerschaft in der Übersetzungstechnologie vorantreiben. Arbeite mit modernen Technologien und bringe Dich in spannende, globale Projekte ein.
  • Langfristige Stabilität: Werde Teil eines Unternehmens mit nachweislicher Erfolgsgeschichte: 22 % unserer Mitarbeitenden sind seit über 10 Jahren bei uns und 27 % seit 5–9 Jahren. Ein Beleg dafür, wie wichtig uns langfristige Bindung und Entwicklung sind.
  • Ein Arbeitsplatz, den man weiterempfiehlt: Wir sind stolz auf unser unterstützendes und wertschätzendes Arbeitsumfeld: Das zeigen unsere 100 % Weiterempfehlungsrate auf Kununu und unsere Zertifizierung als familienfreundliches Unternehmen für 2026.

Warum Du Dich bewerben solltest

Die Entwicklungen im KI-Bereich sind rasant. Bei Plunet ermutigen wir unsere Mitarbeitenden, KI-Tools zu erkunden, sich damit weiterzubilden und sie in ihre Arbeitsabläufe zu integrieren. Für eine Kultur der kontinuierlichen Verbesserung und Anpassung.

Auch wenn wir KI zur Optimierung unserer Prozesse einsetzen, spiegelt unser Recruiting-Prozess unsere Werte wider. Wir legen Wert auf Transparenz und Respekt und konzentrieren uns auf Fähigkeiten, Motivation und Potenzial. Alle Einstellungsentscheidungen bei Plunet werden von Menschen getroffen: Von der Sichtung jedes einzelnen Lebenslaufs bis zur finalen Entscheidung. In Live-Interviews setzen wir keine KI-Tools ein. In den Gesprächen geht es darum, sich gegenseitig kennenzulernen und zu verstehen, wie Bewerberinnen und Bewerber denken, zusammenarbeiten und an unterschiedliche Situationen herangehen. Wir stellen sicher, dass alle Entscheidungen über eine Einstellung von Menschen und nicht von Maschinen getroffen werden.

Diversity & Inclusion
Wir setzen uns für Chancengleichheit, Fairness und gegenseitigen Respekt ein und ermutigen Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Hintergründen, sich zu bewerben.

Anonymer Bewerbungsprozess
Du kannst dich gerne ohne Foto und ohne persönliche Angaben bewerben. Geschlecht, Alter, Name, Familienstand oder Herkunft sind für uns nicht entscheidend.

Überzeuge uns mit deinen Qualifikationen, deinen Fähigkeiten und deiner Motivation, Teil von Plunet zu werden.

Du führst ein Team von sechs Mitarbeitenden, steuerst unser Freelancer-Netzwerk und trägst die Umsatzverantwortung für den gesamten Delivery-Bereich. Dein Auftrag: dafür sorgen, dass unser Wachstum nicht in Überlastung oder Qualitätsverlust kippt, sondern kontrolliert und wirtschaftlich passiert. Du berichtest direkt an den CEO.

Aufgaben

Umsatz und Wirtschaftlichkeit

  • Du verantwortest das Umsatzziel des Delivery-Bereichs und steuerst es monatlich gegen den Plan
  • Du entscheidest, was intern gemacht und was extern eingekauft wird, und behältst dabei die Marge im Blick
  • Du erkennst unbezahlten Mehraufwand früh und stellst ihn ab, statt ihn zu verwalten

Führung und Entwicklung

  • Fachliche und disziplinarische Führung des Delivery-Teams über alle Gewerke hinweg
  • Du entwickelst Menschen weiter, statt Aufgaben nur zu verteilen: du erkennst, was jemand als Nächstes lernen muss, und sorgst dafür, dass es passiert
  • Regelmäßige Leistungsreviews mit klaren Erwartungen, echtem Feedback und dokumentierten Maßnahmen
  • Du erkennst Unterperformance und strukturelle Engpässe früh und handelst, statt zu hoffen
  • Steuerung und Qualitätssicherung unseres Freelancer-Netzwerks

Delivery-Qualität und Kundenzufriedenheit

  • Gesamtverantwortung dafür, dass Projekte sauber, termingerecht und wirtschaftlich rausgehen
  • Du bist die Eskalationsinstanz bei kritischen Projektabweichungen und entscheidest, statt zu moderieren
  • Systematische Reduktion von Rework, Verzögerungen und Qualitätsmängeln durch klare Standards und Abnahmekriterien

Prozesse und Skalierbarkeit

  • Weiterentwicklung und Effizienz aller Delivery-Prozesse
  • Standardisierung dort, wo sie Qualität, Geschwindigkeit und Skalierbarkeit erhöht, und nur dort
  • Du sorgst dafür, dass Workinstructions vollständig, aktuell und im Team verbindlich angewendet werden

Ressourcen und Kapazität

  • Gesamtüberblick über Auslastung, Engpässe und Abhängigkeiten
  • Aktives Gegensteuern bei Überlastung und bei Leerlauf
  • Überstunden sind bei uns kein Steuerungsinstrument

Qualifikation

  • Du hast Delivery, Produktion oder Projektmanagement in einer Agentur oder einem Dienstleistungsunternehmen verantwortet
  • Du hast bereits ein Team geführt und weiterentwickelt, fachlich wie persönlich
  • Du hast Erfahrung darin, externe Dienstleister und Freelancer zu steuern, inklusive Qualität und Kosten
  • Du behältst über mehrere Fachdisziplinen den Überblick, ohne in jeder selbst Expert:in zu sein
  • Ein Umsatzziel zu verantworten ist für dich nichts Neues
  • Auslastungs-, Soll-Ist- und Projektmargenrechnungen liest du ohne fremde Hilfe
  • Du entscheidest auch bei unangenehmen Themen und stehst danach dazu
  • Du unterscheidest den Einzelfall vom strukturellen Problem und behandelst beides unterschiedlich
  • Du sagst Sales auch mal Nein, wenn eine Zusage nicht lieferbar ist
  • Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch, weil unsere Kund:innen Praxen in Deutschland sind

Benefits

  • Echte Entscheidungsbefugnis: Priorisierung, Prozesse, Ressourcen, Budget. Du entscheidest, du musst nicht überzeugen.
  • Klarer Rahmen: Wir arbeiten nach Scaling Up. Ziele, Rhythmen und Verantwortlichkeiten sind schriftlich definiert, nicht Auslegungssache.
  • Weiterentwicklung, die nicht nur im Vertrag steht: Du bekommst ein eigenes Budget für Fortbildung und Coaching und einen festen Rhythmus, in dem wir über deine Entwicklung sprechen, nicht nur über deine Zahlen.
  • Flexible Urlaubsplanung: Du entscheidest, wann du deine Auszeit brauchst. Denn Erholung ist wichtig.
  • 4-Tage-Woche: Unsere Erfahrung zeigt dass eine Arbeitswoche auch in 4 Tagen gelingt.
  • High-End Technik: MacBook & Co. für produktives Arbeiten, natürlich auch zur privaten Nutzung.
  • Urban-Sports, Jobrad & Co.: Deine Fitness und Mobilität liegen uns am Herzen. Ob Urban Sports, Jobrad oder Deutschlandticket, du hast die freie Wahl.

Danach entscheiden wir, und danach wirst du bei uns bewertet.

Das sind unsere fünf Core Values. Sie stehen nicht zur Dekoration hier, sie sind Teil jedes Feedbacks und jeder Beurteilung.

  • Wir spielen auf Sieg. Jeder kennt seine Zahl und findet selbst den Weg dorthin. Auf Anweisungen warten wir nicht.

  • Zufrieden ist zu wenig. Wir liefern, womit niemand gerechnet hat. Unsere Kund:innen empfehlen uns, ohne dass wir fragen.
  • Wir sagen, was wir denken. Scheinharmonie ist Respektlosigkeit in Zeitlupe. Klarheit ist unsere Form von Wertschätzung.

Wenn dich das eher abschreckt als anzieht, sind wir vermutlich nicht die richtige Adresse. Wenn du beim Lesen genickt hast, sollten wir reden.

title: Senior PR Manager (m/w/d) – Remote oder Berlin
description:
Overview

PR steht vor einem strukturellen Bruch. Vertrauen verschiebt sich, Sichtbarkeit wird neu verteilt, KI wächst exponentiell. Wir bei getpress glauben, dass Reputation in den nächsten zehn Jahren der entscheidende Wettbewerbsvorsprung für Unternehmen wird. Und dass die Agentur, die das ernst nimmt, anders aussehen muss als die Agentur von gestern.

Deshalb bauen wir die PR Company der Zukunft. Outcome-getrieben statt Retainer-Stunden. KI-first statt KI-on-top. Automatisiert, wo es skaliert und menschlich, wo es wirklich zählt. Unser über 40 köpfiges Team aus Journalist*innen und PR-Strateg*innen hat seit 2017 die PR für 450+ der spannendsten Wachstumsunternehmen Europas gesteuert – und hat Hunger auf mehr.

Bist du dabei?


Deine Rolle

  • Strategisch und themensicher: Du entwickelst individuelle PR Strategien für Kunden aus dem B2B- und B2C-Bereich – mit klarem Fokus auf Themenplatzierung in relevanten Medien. Dabei bringst du journalistisches Denken und strategische Kommunikation zusammen.
  • Beratend auf Augenhöhe: Du steuerst die Kommunikation mit deinen Kund*innen professionell, planst vorausschauend (z. B. mit Quartalsplänen & KPIs) und baust langfristige Beziehungen auf. Du bringst proaktiv Themen ein – und entwickelst die Kommunikation deiner Kund*innen kontinuierlich weiter. Du bist Sparringspartner*in auf C-Level-Augenhöhe, nicht Auftragsempfänger*in.
  • Teamorientiert & offen: Du teilst dein Wissen, gibst und nimmst Peer-to-Peer-Feedback über alle Erfahrungslevel hinweg, ohne Gatekeeping, mit echtem Interesse an gemeinsamer Weiterentwicklung.
  • Vorne auf der AI Welle: Du arbeitest aktiv mit unserem internen AI-Stack. Recherche, Pitch-Vorbereitung, Themen-Scouting – wo Maschinen schneller sind, lassen wir sie machen. Du investierst die gewonnene Zeit in Substanz, Beziehungen und Kreativität.
  • Aktives Netzwerken: Du baust und pflegst belastbare Beziehungen zu Journalist*innen aus den wichtigsten Medien im DACH Raum und Europas.


Wer du bist

  • 4+ Jahre Erfahrung in der operativen PR, idealerweise im Agenturumfeld, und hast Kund*innen nachweislich eigenständig in deutschen Leit- und Fachmedien platziert.
  • Du bringst fundierte Beratungskompetenz mit, analysierst Zielgruppen und Märkte, übersetzt Unternehmensziele in PR Strategien, leitest messbare Maßnahmen ab und begleitest deine Kund*innen als verlässliche* Sparringspartner*in auf Augenhöhe.
  • Du hast ein belastbares Netzwerk zu Journalist*innen und weißt, wie man vertrauensvolle Beziehungen aufbaut und pflegt.
  • Du beobachtest die Nachrichtenlage aktiv und erkennst Themenpotenziale, bevor andere sie auf dem Schirm haben.
  • Du arbeitest eigenverantwortlich, bringst dich ins Team ein und teilst dein Wissen offen.
  • Du nutzt KI-Tools pragmatisch, um Prozesse zu beschleunigen, damit mehr Zeit für inhaltliche Tiefe und kreative Ideen bleibt.
  • Du sprichst Deutsch auf C2- Niveau, kannst auch auf Englisch professionell kommunizieren und lebst in Deutschland


Was dich erwartet

  • Journalistische PR statt Massenversand: Bei uns gibt es keine generischen Pressemitteilungen oder Gießkannenverteiler. Wir arbeiten individuell, redaktionell und mit klarer Themenstrategie und pitchen gezielt per Telefon bei passenden Journalist*innen aus einem breiten Medienspektrum.
  • Langfristige Perspektive & Entwicklung: Du startest mit einem unbefristeten Vertrag. Gemeinsam entwickeln wir einen klaren Fahrplan für deine fachliche und persönliche Weiterentwicklung – mit regelmäßigen Feedbacks und transparenten Zielen.
  • Flexibilität, die wirklich gelebt wird: Ob remote (innerhalb Deutschlands), hybrid oder im Berliner Office – wir ermöglichen Arbeitsmodelle, die sich mit deinem privaten und beruflichen Leben gut vereinbaren lassen. Entscheidungsfreiheit, Eigenverantwortung und klare Kommunikation gehören für uns selbstverständlich dazu.
  • Unterstützung und offene Arme: Wir begegnen einander auf Augenhöhe – offen, ehrlich und mit echtem Interesse am Gegenüber. Wir lernen voneinander, geben einander Rückhalt und feiern gemeinsame Erfolge.
  • Eine Kultur von Challengern. Wir arbeiten ergebnisgetrieben, feiern Erfolge und erwarten, dass du uns challenged – und wir challengen zurück. Augenhöhe heißt bei uns: ehrliches Feedback in beide Richtungen.
  • Eine Lernkurve, die du anderswo nicht bekommst. Du arbeitest täglich mit einem Team, das das fortschrittlichste AI PR System im Markt baut. Wer sich jetzt einbringt, baut sich ein Profil, das in der Branche selten ist.

Je nach Projekt bedeutet das:

Rund um das „Altersvorsorgedepot“ entstehen in Deutschland neue Marktchancen.

Du bewertest, welche Rolle Zasta darin spielen sollte – von einer Affiliate-Partnerschaft bis zu einer tief integrierten Produktlösung.

Markt & Strategie → Business Case → Partner Sourcing → Verhandlung → MVP → Tech-Integration → Go-live

We are building a new 150 m² studio at Osloer Straße 16–17 in the historic Umspannwerk Christiania, with a workshop and our own exhibition space.

Our cognitive paintings are oil paintings whose images shift with light, movement and sound through custom LED systems and software. Building these paintings and building the new studio are equally important parts of the internship. Both ask us to work with our hands, solve problems together and learn across disciplines.

Our team crosses disciplines: Jonathan Apelbaum (painting and artistic direction), Thore Bartholomäus (co-owner and main engineer), James Calvert (mechanics and mechatronics), Fabian Wetekamp (software), Titouan Duflo (engineering, performance and AV), Clément Royon (music and soundscape) and malice. (a French collective from Clermont-Ferrand), Lucie Froehlich (fabrication and animation), Aysu Naz Atalay (writing), Valeria Loseva (building), and Alexandra Psijas (design). We also work with choreographer Matilde Flor Usinger and musician Forgotten Sounds to shape how an exhibition moves into the night.

Our own series of ambitious, invitation-only exhibitions and events is central to the new studio. We design and build adaptable furniture in steel and oak so the same room can hold work, an exhibition or a dinner. We make the artworks, shape the space, invite our guests and welcome them ourselves. With Clément Royon's music, an exhibition can slowly change its rhythm; with Forgotten Sounds, it can move into a party. This way of working grows from Jonathan's experience in queer and club culture. Beyond the studio, we create large installations with TRACEY (formerly Lunchbox Candy), Playground Festival and other art festivals.

How the internship works

We welcome engineers, programmers, makers, artists, writers and communicators. The internship has three connected parts:

1. We begin together with two equally important jobs: building the studio and building the cognitive paintings. Everyone joins the hands-on work, whatever their background. This includes renovating and making furniture as well as assembling, wiring and testing the paintings.

2. You take on one main studio project shaped around your skills, with guidance from the team. This can become the direction of a longer collaboration.

3. In May, we come together for a major exhibition. We will transform an entire building and take care of the experience from installation and invitations to welcoming guests.

Tasks

  • Build, assemble and test cognitive paintings and their LED systems
  • Build the studio with us, including custom steel and oak furniture and its adaptable exhibition and dining space
  • Contribute to research, prototypes, software, spatial design or storytelling according to your skills
  • Organise materials, tools, storage, artwork transport and installation in the studio and at external sites
  • Manage shipping lists, cost estimates, and customs documentation
  • Write or create invitations, exhibition texts, documentation and communication materials where relevant to your project
  • Assist in managing multiple ongoing projects
  • Occasionally travel as a courier for exhibition

Requirements

  • A practice or strong interest in engineering, programming, making, visual art, writing, communication or related fields
  • Ability to work independently and take initiative
  • Interest in contemporary art, installation, or performance
  • Curiosity about working across art, technology, production, storytelling and communication; you do not need to arrive with all these skills
  • Reliability, flexibility and care for both artworks and people

Benefits

You will learn within a diverse team that works like a chosen family, surrounded by a larger community. You will gain practical experience in electronics, steel and oak, and help shape our studio, intimate events and major May exhibition. Your own studio project gives you room to grow with us.

  • Duration: 6 months
  • Format: Part-time
  • Compensation: Unpaid

You must have paid work outside the studio—whether a job, freelance work or service work—to support yourself during this unpaid internship. An independent artistic project alongside is welcome, but optional. Within Studio Apelbaum, you will lead one main project agreed with and supported by the team.

The studio is a place to teach, learn and grow together. We are looking for people who want to stay with us. The internship is a first step, and the main project you take on here can become the direction of your future work in the studio.

title: Product Manager, Courier Delivery Experience
description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

We seek a Product Manager to join our Courier and Delivery Experience (CDX) team. This role will focus on ensuring world-class courier and consumer delivery experiences while continually evolving the delivery process with a future-oriented mindset. The Courier and Delivery Experience team owns the experiences that elevate every Wolt delivery, from the moment a courier opens the app to every order they accept, all the way to dropping an order off at the customer's doorstep. The team sits at the intersection of a multi-sided marketplace product, real-world operations, and safety, and the work directly moves how reliable Wolt feels to consumers and how satisfied our couriers are when delivering.

You will play a crucial role in shaping the courier experience, ensuring that our couriers feel valued and supported while enhancing the efficiency of deliveries. By blending operational expertise with a deep understanding of courier needs, you will improve the user journey from onboarding couriers to completing deliveries. From designing new features that boost courier satisfaction to refining delivery processes, your work will contribute to key metrics across courier engagement, performance, and satisfaction. You will also be influential in shaping the evolution of the live delivery experience for our courier partners, the merchant courier interaction at pickup and the consumer courier interaction at the doorstep via the Courier app surfaces. 

The ideal candidate will have an exceptional track record in product management, with proven success in working with cross-functional teams across engineering, design, product, and operations. You will define the vision and roadmap for courier and delivery experiences across multiple projects. Working in partnership with business stakeholders, you will also collaborate on cross-team initiatives, contributing to the broader business strategy while ensuring a deep understanding of the courier experience.

Join us in shaping the future of delivery, where every delivery is an opportunity for delight and loyalty.

Our humble expectations

You could come to this role from various backgrounds, but ideally, you bring:

  • Several years of experience in product management, specializing in consumer-facing products
  • Expertise in developing user-centric products, with the ability to address complex user experience-related challenges.
  • Demonstrated expertise in supporting cross-functional teams and fostering operational excellence in fast-paced, high-demand industries.
  • Proven track record in building products influencing cross-functional teams, including engineering, data, design, and operations.
  • High ownership and collaborative capabilities, making thoughtful decisions, and focusing on product details to ensure execution aligns with the vision.
  • Strong ability to define, execute, and measure meaningful OKRs, ensuring alignment with company-wide goals and fostering bottom-up alignment from your team.
  • Ability to focus on the bigger picture, creating solutions that benefit couriers, operations, and customer experiences across the organization.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, able to work effectively with diverse internal teams and external partners, while confidently engaging with leadership in a high-visibility role

The position will be filled as soon as we find the right person, so make sure to apply as soon as you realize you really, really want to join us!

The compensation will be a negotiable combination of monthly pay and DoorDash RSUs. The latter makes it exceptionally easy to be excited about our company growing and doing well, as you'll own a piece of the pie.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

Da wir eine starke B2C-Brand aufbauen wollen, wissen wir, dass wir früh in Brand investieren müssen. Wer in Deutschland ein E-Auto verkaufen will, soll automatisch an Aampere denken und wir suchen die Person, die das für uns umsetzt.
Die Strategie legst du mit dem Head of Marketing fest. Die Umsetzung liegt komplett bei dir, ohne Micro-Management im Tagesgeschäft.

Du planst die Kampagnen und führst sie auch durch. Du entscheidest Umfang, Region, Kanäle und Botschaft, von OOH über YouTube bis PR und Community. Nichts ist vorentschieden. Du testest Regionen gegeneinander und skalierst, was gewinnt.
Du bestimmst, wofür Aampere steht. Aus Research zu Kunden, Markt und Wettbewerb entstehen Positionierung, Narrative und Tone of Voice. Das Fundament gibt es noch nicht, aber die Research dafür würde schon gestartet.
Du denkst über Awareness Kanäle hinaus. Ein großer Teil unserer Brand Wahrnehmung entsteht während des Sales Prozesses. Du denkst vom ersten bis zum letzten Touchpoint der Customer Journey und sorgst in den richtigen Momenten für die richtige Message & Erfahrung.

Das bringst du mit

Du hast eine Brand von null mitgebaut. 4 bis 6 Jahre Brand-Erfahrung im B2C, Startup oder startup-nah. Du hast nicht ein bereits bestehendes System verwaltet, sondern eines aufgebaut.
Du denkst von Konzept bis Go-Live. Du hast Multi-Channel-Kampagnen bereits selbst konzipiert und live gebracht. Du weißt genau, wann welcher Kanal der richtige ist und wie wir unsere Message gezielt an die Kunden übermitteln. Du musst dabei nicht jeden Schritt selbst ausführen, sondern kannst auch auf externe Ressourcen zurückgreifen.

title: Senior Process Engieer
description:
ABOUT US

tozero is Europe’s leading deep-tech startup specializing in the recycling of
lithium-ion batteries. Committed to accelerating decarbonization and transforming
the material life cycle, we’re actively crafting sustainable recycling solutions for a
cleaner and more innovative future.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for a Senior Process Engineer to take a leading technical role in the
design, scale-up, commissioning and ramp up of our battery recycling processes.
This role sits at the intersection of technology development, process engineering,
and industrial scale-up. You will translate experimental and operational data into
robust process designs, challenge engineering assumptions, and ensure that our
future plants are built on solid fundamentals.
Your focus will be on the processes that matter most to our technology — graphite
and lithium extraction. By working closely with R&D, Operations and external
engineering partners, you will actively lead and engage in activities associated with:
a) engineering design; b) commissioning and ramp up; c) process development.
We are looking for someone who is comfortable working in a production
environment, but who can also take a step back and understand what the data is
telling us, and engineer the process we need at different scales.


WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT

Must Have's:
1. Future Plant Design & Scale-up
● Own key process design activities for our next-generation plants.
● Develop and review PFDs, P&IDs, mass and energy balances, process
descriptions and equipment specifications for future capacity expansions.

● Translate pilot and industrial operating data into reliable engineering design
criteria and scale-up assumptions.
● Perform process calculations and equipment sizing to ensure our future
plants are designed based on validated engineering data rather than
theoretical assumptions alone.
2. Targeted Process Expertise & Optimization
● Become a technical reference for some of our most critical process steps.
● Apply strong chemical engineering fundamentals to the optimization of
graphite and lithium extraction and post-processing.
● Identify the parameters controlling yield, purity and process stability and
translate these insights into concrete process improvements.
● Work closely with R&D and Operations while maintaining a strong focus on
process performance and technology development rather than daily
troubleshooting.
3. Data Analysis & Process Modeling
● Turn plant data into engineering decisions.
● Evaluate operational and experimental data, build and validate mass balances
and process models, and identify gaps between expected and actual process
performance.
● Define what data needs to be collected to support future scale-up decisions.
● Technically guide data analysts and other engineering functions to ensure
that models and analytics remain grounded in physical and chemical reality.
● Translate analysis into clear recommendations for process upgrades and
future plant designs.
4. Commissioning & Process Validation
● Make sure what we designed actually works.
● Participate in FATs/SATs, commissioning activities and process performance
validation for new equipment and plant expansions.
● Develop acceptance and process validation criteria based on the original
design intent.
● Evaluate commissioning and operational data to confirm that installed
systems achieve their calculated performance targets.
● Work closely with Operations during handover while ensuring clear ownership
transfers once the process meets its design criteria.
5. Operational Readiness, Process Safety & SOPs
● Design processes that can be operated safely and consistently.
● Translate process design and engineering intent into clear Standard Operating
Procedures (SOPs), operating envelopes and process documentation.
● Participate actively in HAZOPs, LOPAs, and other process safety reviews,
ensuring that process risks are identified and addressed during design rather
than after installation.
● Support Operations in understanding the design basis and critical process
parameters of newly commissioned systems.

Nice-to-have's:
Vendor & EPC Coordination
● Represent tozero's process requirements with external engineering partners
and equipment suppliers.
● Prepare and review technical specifications, vendor proposals and engineering
documentation.
● Challenge unsupported assumptions, identify over-engineered solutions and
ensure equipment is correctly sized for our process.
● Support technical bid evaluations and equipment selection, balancing process
performance, CAPEX, operability and scalability.
● Act as a strong technical counterpart to EPCs, engineering contractors and
equipment vendors throughout project execution.


Your profile

You have a strong chemical/process engineering foundation and enjoy solving
technically complex problems with a combination of first-principles engineering and
real plant data.
● Degree in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Metallurgical
Engineering or a related technical field.
● Ideally 5+ years of experience in process engineering within the chemical,
hydrometallurgy, battery, mining, minerals, recycling or related process
industries; specific expertise in graphite and lithium extraction and
post-processing is highly preferred.
● Strong experience with process design and scale-up, including PFDs, P&IDs,
mass/energy balances and equipment sizing.
● Comfortable working with industrial datasets and translating operational data
into engineering models and decisions.
● Experience with solid-liquid separation, precipitation, flotation,
hydrometallurgy or mineral processing is highly valuable.
● Able to critically review vendor proposals and confidently challenge technical
assumptions.
● Strong experience supporting commissioning and process validation of
industrial equipment or plants.
● Familiarity with process safety methodologies such as HAZOP and LOPA.
● Comfortable moving between detailed calculations, engineering
documentation and the actual plant.
● Strong communicator who can work effectively across R&D, Engineering,
Operations, suppliers and EPC partners.
● Fluent English; German is a plus.


Why us?

Our technology is moving from first-of-a-kind industrial operations toward
increasingly larger and more standardized plants.
The Senior Process Engineer will help us make that transition successfully: turning
what we learn from today's plant into the engineering basis for tomorrow's plants
while supporting commissioning and ramping up efforts.
You will directly influence process performance, equipment selection, CAPEX and the
technical architecture of our future facilities — helping ensure that every new scale is
safer, simpler, more efficient and better engineered than the one before it.

What we do have is a steep growth curve in revenue, a product made in Germany, and a genuine mission: giving the modern office some quiet back.


We have built a strong direct and dealer business on the back of inbound demand and word of mouth. What we have not built yet is a real outbound engine for winning bigger accounts on purpose, from ambitious growth companies to household names like Volkswagen, adidas, IKEA, Red Bull, or Axel Springer, who already trust us today. That gap is this role, and how far into that world you grow is largely up to you.


Outbound is not a new idea for us. We have piloted it in smaller pockets already, testing signal-based outreach and structured sequences with real results. What has been missing is someone to own this as a dedicated motion for bigger accounts rather than a side project squeezed in between other things. That is why we are building this out as a new department and you’d be joining a small, yet focussed team as one of the first hires.


The Role: Build the Pipeline AND the Channel


This is a founding position. You are not stepping into an existing sales org with a quota handed down from three reps before you. You are the first one in the building. What you build, and how you build it, is largely up to you and your team, and you can grow the size and ambition of your target accounts as you find your footing.


  • Green Field, Full Ownership: Build your own pipeline from scratch. There is no inherited book of business and no recycled leads. The customer base you build is yours, and so is the revenue you generate from it.

  • Your Stack, Your Sequences: Clay, Reply.io, LinkedIn Premium, and Aircall are all at your disposal. You design your own outreach sequences, run your own cold calling campaigns, and decide how the machine works. Nobody hands you a script.

  • Segment Strategy, Together: You understand the market as well as anyone. Rather than being handed a target list from above, you and your manager will decide together which segments and account types are worth focusing on.

  • Comp That Rewards More Than the First Deal: An uncapped bonus with a kicker for overperformance. Returning customers you bring in keep feeding your comp over time, not just the initial close. Landing an account well is worth more than landing it once.

  • A Brand That Opens Doors: You are not cold-calling on behalf of an unknown startup. mute-labs is an established, well-regarded market leader with a reference list that already includes some of the biggest names in German and European business. That credibility is yours to use from day one.

  • A seasoned team to back you up: Your manager has built and run outbound and enterprise sales hands-on, from cold pipeline to six-figure closes, and will work closely with you from day one, coaching, supporting, and training wherever it's actually needed rather than just checking in on numbers.


Is This You?


  • The Go-Getter: You do not wait to be told what to do next. You get on your feet quickly, figure out the shape of the problem, and start moving before anyone has to push you.

  • Sales Experience: You have carried a full sales cycle before, from first contact to signed contract, and know how to keep a deal moving without needing someone else to close it for you. You do not need to have sold into large enterprises already, that is something you will grow into here.

  • Stakeholder Management: You know how to work a deal with more than one person in the room, decision-makers, influencers, and budget holders, and you can keep several of those relationships moving in parallel without losing the thread.

  • Comfortable with Ambiguity: There is no existing playbook to inherit here. You will help write it. If you need every process defined for you before you can start, this is not the role.

  • Fluent in German and English: Most of your target accounts are DACH-based, though the reference list extends across the EU. Strong German is expected; English is the internal working language.


Our Hiring Process


We keep this fast and honest, on both sides.


  1. The Spark: A short intro call with our People team to check for basic fit.

  2. The deepdive: A conversation with your future manager Patrick about your experience, how you build your pipeline and how you close. Here you’ll also meet the rest of the team.

  3. The Live Action: A live discovery or negotiation role-play based on a realistic enterprise scenario. No prep deck, just show us how you actually work a deal.

  4. The Vision: A final conversation with Leah, Head of Sales as well as Franziskus, Managing Director, on the strategic mandate behind this role and where it can go from here.


ABOUT US

mute-labs exists to make quiet a normal part of the modern workplace. A few things that set us apart:


  • We are "no tech": we build and sell real hardware, sound-insulated phone and meeting booths that companies actually need.

  • We have no investors, and we are not looking for any. We have been profitable since day one.

  • We are on a steep growth curve, measured in revenue and profit, not headcount for its own sake.

  • We are not building toward an exit. We are building a company meant to last for generations.

title: SAP Account Executive (m/w/d)
description:
Deine Aufgaben

Du weißt, dass du zu den Besten gehörst.  Dein Umfeld weiß es auch.  Aber deine aktuelle Rolle gibt dir nicht mehr den Raum, den du verdienst.   Du hast in den letzten Jahren Deals geschlossen, die andere für unmöglich hielten. Du kennst das SAP-Ökosystem nicht aus Präsentationen – sondern aus echten Co-Sell-Gesprächen, aus Partnerverhandlungen, aus Abschlüssen, die du persönlich über die Linie gebracht hast.  Jetzt fragst du dich: Gibt es eine Rolle, die meinem Anspruch wirklich gerecht wird?   Die gibt es. Und du liest sie gerade. 

Die Rolle

 Dies ist eine reine New-Business-Position mit klarer strategischer Bedeutung für Implicos Wachstum in SAP-zentrierten Prozessindustrien. Du verantwortest die Gewinnung neuer Kundenlogos in den Segmenten Landwirtschaft, Bergbau, Chemie sowie Zement und Baustoffe – in enger Co-Sell-Partnerschaft mit SAP Account Teams und Industry Business Units.  Du bewegst dich in einem Umfeld, in dem Vertrauen, Substanz und Marktkenntnisse entscheiden – nicht Lautstärke. 
 
Deine Verantwortung

  • Vollständige Quota-Verantwortung für neues ARR aus Prozessindustrie-Kunden
  • Identifikation und Qualifizierung von Opportunities aus der SAP-ADRM-Pipeline sowie dem eigenen Netzwerk
  • Aufbau und Pflege belastbarer Co-Sell-Beziehungen mit SAP SCM Sales Reps und IBU-Kontakten
  • Steuerung komplexer Sales-Zyklen von 3–9 Monaten mit mehreren Entscheidungsträgern auf IT-, Operations- und C-Level-Ebene
  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Solution Architects für technische Deep Dives und Proof-of-Value-Definitionen
  • Akkurate Pipeline-Führung im CRM sowie strukturiertes Forecasting
  • Kontinuierliche Rückmeldung von Markt- und Wettbewerbsinformationen an Product- und GTM-Teams


Dein Profil

Was wir voraussetzen:

  • Mindestens 5 Jahre B2B-Softwarevertrieb, davon mindestens 3 Jahre im SAP-Umfeld oder im strukturierten Co-Sell mit SAP
  • Nachweisliche Hunter-Bilanz: nachhaltig neue Kundenbeziehungen aufgebaut und abgeschlossen – nicht primär im Bestandsgeschäft
  • Tiefes Verständnis der SAP Channel- und Co-Sell-Mechanismen: Partnerdeals, RISE/GROW-Pipeline, SAP-Partnerökosystem
  • Erfahrung in der Steuerung von Multi-Stakeholder-Prozessen auf Entscheiderebene
  • Souveränes Auftreten auf C-Level – verbindlich, präzise, auf Augenhöhe
  • Ausgeprägte Eigenständigkeit in einem frühen, sich entwickelnden Go-to-Market-Setup
  • Verhandlungssichere Kenntnisse in Deutsch und Englisch
Was dich zusätzlich auszeichnet:
  • Branchenwissen in Landwirtschaft, Bergbau, Chemie oder Zement/Baustoffe
  • Bestehendes Netzwerk in der SAP SCM- oder Logistik-IBU-Community
  • Erfahrung im Vertrieb von SAP-Add-ons oder SolEx-Produkten
  • Vertrautheit mit Supply-Chain-Execution-, TM- oder Bulk-Logistik-Prozessen
 
Was du bei uns findest
  • Eine strategisch bedeutsame Rolle mit direktem Einfluss auf das Unternehmenswachstum
  • Klare Ziele, volle Autonomie in der Ausführung – kein Mikromanagement
  • Ungedeckeltes Vergütungsmodell – dein Upside spiegelt deinen Beitrag
  • Direkter Zugang zum SAP-Ökosystem und enge Zusammenarbeit mit erfahrenen Solution Architects
  • Ein Umfeld, das Seniorität respektiert und Eigenverantwortung erwartet
Du gestaltest – nicht nur mit. Du gestaltest, wie es wird.

 Implico ist kein fertig gebautes Konstrukt, das auf einen weiteren Vertriebsmitarbeiter wartet. Diese Rolle ist eine der ersten ihrer Art – du definierst mit, wie wir in den Prozessindustrien wahrgenommen werden, wie wir co-sellen, wie wir skalieren. Was du heute aufbaust, bleibt. Dein Fingerabdruck ist sichtbar – in der Kundenbasis, in der Marktpositionierung, in der Art, wie das Team in zwei Jahren arbeitet. Das ist kein Job. Das ist ein Gestaltungsauftrag.
 
Das Team – kein Versprechen, sondern eine Einladung.

 "Tolles Team" steht in jeder Stellenanzeige. Das überspringst du längst. Deshalb sagen wir es anders: Schau dir an, mit wem du zusammenarbeiten würdest.  Mark, Maurice, Anna, Thales, Selina und mehr. Menschen, die nicht wegen des Titels hier sind. Die morgens mit echtem Interesse an ihre Arbeit gehen. Die füreinander einspringen, ohne dass jemand fragen muss. Die über ihre Themen sprechen, als wären es ihre eigenen Projekte – weil sie es sind. Keine perfekte Hochglanz-Kultur. Aber eine, in der Leidenschaft und Haltung mehr zählen als Hierarchie.  Ob das zu dir passt? Das findest du nur heraus, wenn du das Gespräch suchst.
 
Der nächste Schritt

 Wenn du in den letzten Jahren bewiesen hast, dass du im SAP-Umfeld neue Märkte erschließt und Abschlüsse bringst dann freuen wir uns auf ein erstes, offenes Gespräch.  Kein langes Anschreiben. Zeig uns deinen Track Record – der Rest ergibt sich.

Company Description

Since its creation in 2007 in the financial city of Frankfurt am Main, Solactive AG has grown to one of the key players in the indexing space. The German multi-asset index provider focusses on tailor-made indices, offering to its clients a faster service, with greater flexibility and at a reasonable cost. Solactive AG and its subsidiaries have become one of the fastest growing index providers over the past few years and support the leading investment banks and asset managers across the globe. We have gained global recognition for our role in the Exchange Traded Fund (ETF) industry, where we rank among the top providers worldwide for underlying indices. The impact and value we bring to the market is palpable, but also in the reputation we have proudly built by being close to our customers, solidifying Solactive AG as a trusted and reliable ally in the ever-evolving global financial landscape.


Job Overview

Solactive's Aggregate team owns the intraday calculation of our indices: consuming live price streams, applying calculation logic across a wide range of indices, and producing a continuous output stream of index ticks throughout the trading day. The core platform is built in Java and engineered around throughput, latency, and correctness under concurrency, while custom business integrations are built in Python. As a Working Student you join a small team and contribute real, production-bound code to both, working alongside senior engineers who review your work and coach you.


Your Tasks

  • Implement well-scoped features and fixes in the Java calculation platform, such as improvements to calculation components, price stream consumption, or index tick production
  • Write unit, integration, and performance tests, including tests for concurrent code paths where ordering and timing matter
  • Help investigate correctness or performance issues: reproduce them, narrow them down, and propose fixes with senior guidance
  • Build and maintain Python integrations for business teams: connectors to the calculation platform, output adapters, validation checks, and small operational tools
  • Contribute to monitoring and developer tooling that makes calculation behaviour observable and easier to reason about
  • Take part in design and code reviews, ask questions, and document what you learn so the next person can pick it up faster


Your Profile

  • Enrolled student in computer science, software engineering, or a closely related field
  • Strong Java fundamentals: object-oriented design, collections, generics, and comfort reading and writing idiomatic modern Java
  • Solid grounding in core computer science: data structures, algorithms, and complexity, and in particular a working understanding of multithreading and concurrency (threads, synchronisation, memory visibility, races and deadlocks)
  • Openness to Python: no prior experience needed, but willingness to pick it up for integration and tooling work alongside Java
  • Familiarity with Git, the command line, and a testing mindset; interest in measuring performance rather than guessing at it
  • Ability to work independently on a scoped task, ask for help early when stuck, and communicate clearly in writing
  • Available for 15–20 hours per week during the semester, more during semester breaks
  • Interest in financial markets, market data, or index calculation is welcome but not required


Our Offer

  • Be part of the Solactive family  an international FinTech environment with flat hierarchies, real ownership, and strong growth opportunities.
  • Enjoy attractive benefits such as team events, Corporate Benefits access, a modern ergonomic office,free beverages and fruit.
  • Work on a real, high-impact production platform and contribute to architectural improvements not just feature tickets.
  • Gain hands-on experience with Java microservices, build systems, and dependency governance while collaborating with experienced engineers.
  • Build practical backend engineering skills that directly support your long-term career development.

description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

 

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

 

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

 

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

 

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

 

The Role

BJAK is building a Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia. As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.

 

This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges.

 

We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved.

 

What you'll be doing

  • Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.

  • Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.

  • Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.

  • Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.

  • Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.

  • Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.

  • Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.

     

What you'll need

  • Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.

  • Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

  • Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).

  • AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.

  • Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

     

Outcomes

  • Clear vertical strategy and legible roadmap

  • Ships fast and clears the gates that actually block launch

  • Money is correct and users are never misled about the state of their funds

  • AI features are valuable, predictable and trusted

  • Trade-offs made deliberately under uncertainty and hold up when challenged

  • Engineering, design, compliance, and operations are aligned with minimal friction

     

Location

This role is remote, but candidates must be based in Germany. We are hiring specifically for this market, so applicants should already be based in Germany.

 

Language

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

 
 

Interview Process

2. Role-specific interview

For strong candidates, we aim to complete the process and make an offer within 1 week from the start of the interview process. Candidates who complete assessments quickly will be prioritized.

title: Senior Ground Software Engineer
description:
Help Build Europe's Hypersonic Capability
 
At Hypersonica, we’re redefining what’s possible in European defence technology. We exist to deliver speed, resilience, and technological independence at a pace that sets a new standard. We are a small, elite team working on problems that matter, and solving them fast.
 
By joining Hypersonica, you’re not stepping into a predefined role. You’re joining a talent dense environment where every individual shapes the direction of the company. Our philosophy is to hire a small number of exceptional people with broad, deep technical capability, strong judgement, and the ability to operate autonomously.
 
We hire for talent, not rigid boxes. This role represents a business need, but the way it evolves will be shaped by the individual. If you’ve achieved what others said was impossible, or you bring a unique combination of skills that doesn’t fit a traditional mould, we want to hear from you. The work you do here directly contributes to Europe’s technological independence.

What you'll do

  • Design and develop ground software used for mission preparation, execution, and monitoring of hypersonic systems. 

  • Build robust, user facing applications for Linux and Windows environments that support operators and engineers during real missions. 

  • Implement high performance C++ software with a focus on reliability, usability, and maintainability. 

  • Develop intuitive user interfaces and workflows to visualise system state, mission data, and operational status. 

  • Integrate ground software with simulation, test, and live system interfaces to support end to end operations. 

  • Work closely with systems, GNC, test, and operations teams to translate mission needs into effective software tools. 

  • Where useful, leverage UI frameworks (e.g. Qt) and mapping or visualisation SDKs to accelerate development. 


Who you are

  • A Senior software engineer with 5+ years’ experience building ground or operator-facing software in aerospace, defence, or complex technical domains. 

  • Comfortable developing user-facing applications on Linux and Windows, with an understanding of operational reliability. 

  • Fluent in modern C++, with an instinct for performance, robustness, and clean architecture. 

  • Someone who cares deeply about operator experience, clarity, and usability in high-pressure environments. 

  • Experienced translating mission and system needs into practical software tools, not just features. 

  • Pragmatic about tooling, with exposure to UI frameworks such as Qt and an interest in visualisation or mapping technologies. 

  • Able to move quickly in a startup environment, balancing polish with delivery speed. 

  • Motivated by building software that operators trust during real missions, not demo-only systems. 


What we offer

  • A mission driven environment with the opportunity to work on one of Europe’s most consequential defence challenges, with direct impact on sovereign capability and security. 

  • Daily collaboration with top experts across engineering, operations, and defence, with real opportunity to learn from the best, contribute, and grow. 

  • High ownership and autonomy; no time tracking, no micromanagement, just clear objectives and accountability for outcomes. 

  • A fast paced environment where good ideas are implemented quickly, and feedback from test and flight drives real decisions. 

  • A culture that values clarity, integrity, and excellence, and supports people who take initiative and push boundaries responsibly. 

  • Competitive compensation and real share options aligned to responsibility and impact, not tenure or hierarchy. 

At Hypersonica, every hire raises the bar. We are deliberately small, intensely capable, and deeply mission-driven. If this role feels like a strong fit, or if you believe you bring something exceptional that goes beyond the description, we encourage you to apply.
 
Hypersonica is an equal-opportunity employer and assesses candidates solely on merit, capability, and potential.
 
You can apply directly to this role or reach out to Nathan Sweeney, Head of Talent. We review every application and aim to respond to all candidates within two weeks, whether the answer is yes or no.

Founded in 2017, RoomPriceGenie is dedicated to helping hoteliers around the globe achieve optimal pricing. 🌍 We understand that many small hotels face challenges with digitalization, making their operations increasingly complex and often resulting in lost revenue. This is where we come in!

Now, we are excited to expand our customer base and spread the word about how we can support hoteliers in optimizing their pricing strategies. We invite you to join us on this journey! We actively encourage applications from candidates with diverse backgrounds to enrich our team and drive innovation.

Your Role

As the Head of UX at RoomPriceGenie, you'll lead our small but mighty design and research team of two product designers and one user researcher.

This isn't an IC role where you'll be pushing pixels or running sessions yourself. It's a leadership role focused on building the function, championing the team, and setting them up for success.

You'll set the strategic direction for how design and research operates, advocate for the team at leadership level, and create the conditions for your people to do their best work. You'll also play a key role in raising design and research maturity across the wider product organisation — guiding better decisions through clearer systems, guidelines, and shared insight.

Key Responsibilities

Leadership Representation & Advocacy

  • Champion design and research as a strategic partner that shapes the roadmap.

  • Partner with Product Leadership to translate strategic business priorities into a clear, sequenced roadmap for Design & Research.

Strategic Direction & Vision

  • Set a clear vision for the design and research function — defining what success looks like, where it's heading, and how it contributes to the company's overall strategy.

  • Raise design and research maturity by providing constructive critique and quality oversight to support high-quality product outcomes.

  • Create the space for the team to work on foundational initiatives that scale team impact. For example: evolving the component library into a robust design system and establishing clear design and content playbooks to drive consistency, efficiency, and quality.

AI Operations & Enablement

  • Set the strategic direction for how AI fits into the design & research workflow — where it accelerates, where craft stays human, and set clear guardrails for how the wider org uses it.

  • Foster a culture where the team integrates AI into product work — evolving their craft and building fluency through practice.

  • Ensure designers and researchers play a key role in shaping product and AI direction, grounding decisions in user insight and design perspective.

Stakeholder Collaboration

  • Advocate for Design Thinking to be embedded throughout the product life cycle, shaping ideas and guiding decisions.

  • Proactively identify large, strategic UX opportunities that span across the product.

  • Navigate competing priorities between leadership direction and team capacity, ensuring the team stays focused on high-impact work.

Team Development & Coaching

  • Provide ongoing coaching, mentoring, and constructive feedback through regular one-to-ones — focused on the development and growth of your team.

  • Build clear career frameworks and progression paths for Design and Research.

  • Encourage continuous learning, adaptability, and development within the team.

Your Profile

  • A genuine understanding of both design and research disciplines, even if your background leans more toward one. You don't need to be an expert in both, but you need to value and support both equally.

  • Proven experience in a senior design leadership role is required — you've owned a function, led teams of designers and researchers, and have a track record of influencing product direction at the leadership level.

title: Full Stack Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
TL;DR

Join GlassDollar and help build the system some of Europe's largest companies use to find, test, and adopt startup technology.
We're looking for an engineer who wants considerably more responsibility than "implement what's in the ticket". You'll take an ambiguous problem, shape it together with product, make the important technical decisions, ship it, and stay close enough to see whether it worked.
We expect you to have opinions. We also expect you to be good enough to change them.

The problem we're solvingLarge organisations are remarkably good at accumulating problems. A company with 100,000 employees can have thousands of operational challenges across its business units. Somewhere outside that organisation, a startup has probably already built part of the solution. Getting those two things to meet still happens through spreadsheets, long email threads, and meetings whose primary output is another meeting.
GlassDollar OS is the operating system for venture clienting: problem → startup discovery → evaluation → PoC → adoption, in one repeatable workflow.
Our customers are some of Europe's largest organisations, so the software has to move quickly and behave like something an enterprise can depend on. That tension creates the interesting engineering problems.



What we're looking for

You can take a problem further than the ticket. Work often starts with something incomplete, like "customers need a better way to manage X". You'll shape the problem with product, challenge assumptions, and decide what belongs in this iteration. Strong opinions about what we build, not only how, are expected here.

You care about product. You want to know who you're building for, why the problem matters, and what success looks like. That context should shape your technical decisions.

You have technical judgement. There is rarely one correct architecture. You know when the boring solution beats the ambitious one, when an abstraction helps and when it hides the problem, and when a small feature is about to create six months of technical debt. We expect you to reason about API boundaries, data models, permissions, performance, failure modes, testing, observability, and rollout, and to raise concerns with a clear argument attached.

You make the system better, not just the feature. You fix the spreading pattern rather than the single instance, make an API easier for the next person, and improve tests because the current setup makes everyone afraid to deploy. Your impact should show beyond the pull requests with your name on them.

You can work across the stack. A feature might run from a React interaction through GraphQL into a Node service, a schema redesign, a permissions update, and a safe migration for existing customers. Curiosity to follow the problem matters more than equal depth everywhere.

You own quality. We have QA. That's not where quality begins. What breaks if this request happens twice? What happens with old data, or when the API fails halfway through? We use Playwright and Jest alongside reviews and monitoring. The goal isn't coverage, it's confidence.

You communicate like your decisions will matter later. Six months from now, somebody should understand an important decision without digging through seventeen Slack messages and a deleted Notion comment. That means writing things down when they matter, explaining trade-offs clearly, giving useful code reviews, and surfacing risks before they become incidents.

You raise the engineering bar around you. You do not need a management title to have influence. Find the hole in an architecture, unblock someone without taking the keyboard away, disagree without turning every decision into a referendum. As you earn trust, you’ll naturally become the person people bring harder problems to.



What you'll do

Over your first year:

  • Enterprise integrations: into our customers' systems, data, identity providers, and workflows. This is what turns GlassDollar from software somebody logs into, into infrastructure their organisation operates on.
  • APIs and MCP: public REST APIs and MCP servers for our customers, their engineers, and increasingly their AI agents. The interesting part isn't exposing endpoints, it's designing an external platform we'll still be happy supporting years from now.
  • AI inside real workflows: embeddings, vector search, and LLMs across a large database of startups and corporate innovation data. We're less interested in adding a ✨ button to everything than in finding places where AI removes real work.
  • Workflow automation: triggers, notifications, and automation that replace humans moving information between systems.
  • Core product engineering: React interfaces, APIs, PostgreSQL queries, permissions, migrations, performance work, and the occasional bug whose root cause makes everybody stare silently at their screen.
Our stack
  • Frontend: TypeScript, React, Material UI, Apollo Client, Playwright
  • Backend: Node.js, GraphQL, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Jest
  • Infrastructure: AWS, Terraform, GitHub Actions, Sentry
  • Increasingly: LLM APIs, embeddings, vector search, MCP, AI-assisted engineering workflows
You don't need experience with every item. Reasoning about systems matters more to us than having memorised our exact stack.


Requirements

  • Substantial production experience with TypeScript, React, and Node.js
  • Comfortable reasoning about relational databases, not just the ORM
  • Can independently take a feature from unclear starting point to production
  • Can read unfamiliar code without immediately proposing a rewrite

Nice to have:
  • Experience with GraphQL, Prisma, or PostgreSQL at scale
  • Exposure to LLM APIs, embeddings, or vector search
  • Experience owning systems, not just features
Don't check every box? Apply anyway. We'd rather have the conversation than lose someone over a bullet point.


How we hire

How we workWe're a small engineering team, so there are fewer places for responsibility to disappear and no chain of five people between you and a decision. We prefer written context over meetings the calendar invented, and working software over elaborate process.
Quickly doesn't mean carelessly. Sometimes the fastest route is the simple version today, sometimes it's another day on a foundation twenty future features will sit on. Knowing which situation you're in is part of the job. Expect to ship to production very early.

How we hireNo seven-stage endurance test. No algorithm trivia disconnected from the work.

  1. Intro. You, us, and whether this is the environment you're actually looking for.
  2. Technical conversation. We go deep on something difficult you've built: the decisions, the alternatives, what you'd do differently now.
  3. Technical assessment. Usually live coding on a realistic problem, sometimes a small proof of concept instead. We care how you think, not whether your solution matches ours.
  4. Offer. If there's strong mutual conviction, we move.

One last thingJob descriptions have a habit of producing candidates who optimise themselves against bullet points. Please don't. If you're reading this thinking "I can do most of this, but I haven't worked with MCP", apply.
Strong fundamentals, meaningful software shipped, and a bias toward ownership are what we're looking for. The rest is learnable.

title: Senior Conversion Design Analyst (f/m/d)
description:
Your mission

We're looking for a Senior Conversion Design Analyst who decides with evidence. You will frame real user problems based on qualitative and quantitative data, design a part of our product, form a view about what should change, build the experiment that tests it, and analyze the results yourself. 

You will sit inside the product delivery team that focuses on user growth, working closely with the person accountable for that part of the business and with the engineers building it. And you will not be doing it alone: You join a group of Conversion Design Analysts across the company who work the same way and hold each other's standards.

English is our working language. German matters here too: You will be designing flows that German-speaking users read.

Concretely, you will:

  • Design experiences grounded in real user needs and real neighbourhood life. Your job is to design flows and screens that are highly usable and intuitive and that earn their place by adding measurable value, not just because we can build them.

  • Frame the real problem before solving it. Dig into quantitative and qualitative data until you find the actual question underneath the ask. Then make it explainable and actionable. A well-framed problem is half the battle

  • Run the experiment, and read it honestly. Design a testable change, get it instrumented properly, and analyse the outcome. That includes reporting the tests that did not work, and saying what you would do differently.

  • Talk to neighbours. Experiments tell you what happened, not what people needed. You will spend real time with the people who use this, because you cannot A/B test your way to understanding somebody.

  • Direct AI, and spend your judgment where it counts. AI produces a lot of our first-pass design. You will brief it, push back on it, and hold the quality bar, so your own hours go to the thinking a model cannot do. 

  • Argue for cutting things. Adding is easy. You will help decide what earns its place and what should be removed, and be willing to make the case for less.


Your profile

  • You practice product design and analytics. You might come from an analyst background and bring a love of design and design thinking, or vice versa.

  • You have technical know-how and experience in setting up and evaluating experiments in an A/B testing tool, constructing the needed dashboards for the problem space you are working on and use our design system tooling.

  • With sufficient data literacy, you get your own numbers through SQL query. You work with raw data to dig up insights and spot opportunities, without waiting for someone else to pull it for you.

  • You have run experiments end to end: set up the hypothesis, decide on the right metrics to track, design the test variants, analyze the results, decide on how to continue. 

  • You have statistical literacy. You don’t need to be able to run R, but you understand what Bayesian vs. frequentist is about and why you do a power analysis before launching an experiment. 

  • You care about craft and are attentive to details. You can tell the difference between good enough and actually good and you design experiences people do not have to think about.

  • You are fluent with AI tools. This role allows you to have more control and impact through both design and analysis, but to do this well you'll need to leverage (and at times extend) our AI enablement stack

  • You present your work clearly, defend your decisions when challenged, and are comfortable in front of a crowd.

  • Excellent English skills for working in our international team.

To apply, share a portfolio that shows your work by impact — at least one project walked through end to end: the hypothesis, what you designed, the result, and what you took from it. Show us how you used data to move your thinking forward, and where experimentation shaped what you built. 

Nice to have

  • Experience with a marketplace, community, classifieds, or other network product.

  • Experience building or maintaining parts of a design system. 

  • Comfortable writing SQL without AI assistance.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

Location

This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with occasional visits to customers across the DACH region.

As team collaboration is of great importance to us, we highly encourage team members to join us in Zurich at least once a month. These visits are financially supported by BLP.

About the role

For a process to run autonomously, four things have to line up: the technology, the process itself, the data behind it, and the people who work with it. That alignment does not happen at go-live. It happens in the months after, and that is where this role sits.

Our customers go live with a working solution. What they do not have on day one is an organisation that operates in an AI-native way. Processes were designed around people checking things. Data was maintained well enough for humans to interpret. Teams know the old workarounds better than the new system. Your job is to lead that transition, from a process that is automated in parts to a process that genuinely runs on its own.

That means working across every level of the customer's organisation. With operational teams you build understanding and find where automation is actually blocked. With department leads you challenge the process rules that make full automation impossible, and drive the decisions that change them. And you use the right lever for each blocker, because they are all different: some are a data clean-up you coordinate with the customer, some are a training and adoption gap, some need a custom agent, and some are structural and belong with our engineering teams.

You do not do this alone. You enable the customer's core team to solve their own issues, you work with our Customer Success Engineers on the technical side, and you use the Customer Success Manager to get decisions made where you need commercial weight. For our smaller customers, where there is no Customer Success Manager, you are the escalation point yourself.
